articles.title: Grading Every NHL Hometown Remix Jersey After Reveal
articles.summary: After waiting (mostly) patiently for the past few months, the NHL unveiled its Hometown Remix jerseys. All 32 teams are represented with their own takes on what makes them stand out.
articles.body:
After waiting (mostly) patiently for the past few months, the NHL unveiled its Hometown Remix jerseys. All 32 teams are represented with their own takes on what makes them stand out.

Team names, locales, regional pride, and history are all on display in their own unique ways... for the most part. When it comes to jerseys, we've all got opinions. Some teams went all the way out to impress, while others could've used a bit more consultation.

Whatever the case, we've got grades to hand out for each team. As far as league-wide releases go, this one is a banger, and there's a lot to like. Fortunately, there's a lot to roast as well, so it won't just be all roses for everyone. Let's get the red pens out and dish out the grades.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

An absolute knockout of a jersey for the Ducks.

Anaheim threw it all the way back to the movie that helped bring about the name of the franchise and used the jersey style from The Mighty Ducks and put their own masked duck crest on the front.

You can complain about how the colors aren't technically correct all you want, but the jersey is very much about the Mighty Ducks. It's a pitch-perfect jersey that fully embraces the spirit of what doing a Hometown Remix was supposed to be.

The Bruins took it back to school for their Hometown Remix, and it made for a great idea.

A brown and gold jersey with "BRUINS" in block letters across the front is wholly in the spirit of any college hockey jersey you'll find from any of the NCAA teams in the Boston area. Be it BU, BC, Northeastern, Harvard, or points beyond in the region, this style of jersey has been done in kind.

The Bruins embracing college hockey style like this is a fun idea, even if it comes off a bit bland at first blush. That said, throwing it back with the old team colors and the college-style shield on the shoulders is great.

When the Sabres had a white "goathead" jersey for the Reverse Retro program years ago that used blue and gold highlights, fans in Buffalo wondered when, if ever, there might be a blue and gold "goathead" added to the mix.

Now is that time, and it's done with a lot of special Buffalo touches.

The electric gold on the blue jersey with gold and white stripes plays well into the Sabres color scheme, and the shoulder logo that originally had a sabre piercing the letter "B" is altered with an electric-bolt sabre through the "B." The white stripe on the jersey's sleeves and waist has a star and electric bolt design through it that ties into the City of Buffalo's flag.

Buffalo is known as the "City of Light," and that's what this beautiful jersey represents so well.

Report Card Grades for Every Team's 1st Month 🔠

The thing with Flames jerseys is you don't want to mess with a good thing. The team logo is perfect, and so are the colors. Making the flaming "C" gold with a saddle-shaped waistline hem not only puts a new shine on the Flames, but it also pays homage to the Saddledome, Calgary's home arena, which is in its final season.

There are details included in the Flames' logo and in the sleeve stripes that take into account the texture of the Saddledome's ceiling on the logo and the Dome's windows on the sleeves. It is honestly such a deep cut of a detail; it's as unexpected as it is impressive.

This is a jersey made with love for the home arena and respect for such a perfect logo and jersey.

A lot of fans are deeply confused about seeing the team's mascot, Stormy, on the front, decked out in a classic varsity sweater and a porkpie hat from the 1950s. If you know ball (or jerseys, rather), you're familiar with this iteration of Stormy, and if you've read our takes, you know we've wanted to see it on a jersey front and center.

Wishes do come true, and you know what? We dig it. It's different, it's new, and it's having fun. The shoulder logos highlight parts of North Carolina's flag, as well as a nod to the architecture in Raleigh. The sleeves have oak leaf details in the red stripes since Raleigh is the City of Oaks.

This jersey is definitely not for everyone, but it's very specifically for Hurricanes fans in Raleigh, and that kind of appreciation probably isn't as well met outside of the Research Triangle.

We have a lot of questions here that, thankfully, the marketing details answer.

The green Blackhawks jersey is meant to give the fans what they've wanted since the past St. Patrick's Day special jerseys made them want to see it more often.

Of course, a green Blackhawks jersey is almost an exact replica of a University of North Dakota jersey before they changed the name of the team. Those jerseys were big hits in Chicago thanks to Jonathan Toews being a North Dakota alum and 'Hawks star, but seeing this for the NHL team is rather jarring.

They say the green is meant to represent progress, and the sleeves have four six-pointed stars embedded in them to represent the City of Chicago flag, and that's a cool touch, but you can't help but wonder if using the flag itself as an inspiration for a jersey might work so much better.

The Avalanche opted to better represent their namesake for the Hometown Remix, and an icy, snowy-looking team from Colorado really hits hard.

The white jersey with the icy blue sleeve stripes and a darker cold blue to represent the mountains higher up on the arms is a fun design touch, and using their alternate jersey logo as a crest, which comes from the Colorado state flag, works well for this, particularly with the frosted Avalanche logos on the shoulders.

The silver stripes on the sleeves shimmer which adds to the icy effect they want this jersey to embody. These look simple, but they're eye-catching all the same.

The trouble with being named after a color is that it kind of holds you to needing to use that color all the time. For the Columbus Blue Jackets, finding new ways to use blue is undoubtedly a challenge.

But being called the Blue Jackets presents another issue in that, thanks to the sourcing of the American Civil War for the team's nickname, it would also eliminate the color of the opposition. In this case, the color gray should be a no-go.

Should be. Instead, the Blue Jackets used their fantastic Stadium Series jerseys and flipped around the colors, and unfortunately, that's made gray the main color and blue a highlight color. The gray is meant to help the cannon on the front stand out proudly...but it's gray! The antithesis color for the reason for the team's name!

Sigh. We want to love this because it's a great-looking jersey, but it just couldn't be gray, and it very much is. That's not even taking into account how gray hockey jerseys just don't do so well in the first place, but especially when the team is called the Blue Jackets.

The Stars' Hometown Remix jersey is meant to represent the city skyline and the nightlife of Dallas. With a white-based jersey to help the livened-up Stars logo, as well as the gussied-up sleeve stripes, it's got a lot of modern-esque pizzazz to it.

The logo on the front is textured, and the sleeves have designs debossed within the black stripes. This jersey feels almost like a total flip on the "blackout" alternate they had until recently, which had neon green for the stripes, name, number, and logo, but with a few more little touches to make it stand out better.

This is a fine jersey, if not underwhelming. We understand that throwing stars all over it might've been a bit over the top.

Haven't Red Wings fans been through enough?

After hitting a grand slam with their centennial jersey last year (which became their alternate this season), the Hometown Remix falls desperately flat.

It's simple, which is what the Red Wings' standard jerseys are, and that's fine. But taking that jersey and throwing "Hockeytown" above the winged wheel and calling it a day is so dull it's almost unhinged.

The most fun thing about this is the octopus-tentacle design on the hem on the inside of the jersey. If you buy one, you'll see it. If you don't, you'll probably never know it's there. For a team with a great legacy with their jerseys, seeing alternates so regularly end up disappointing is a huge let-down.

You want to dislike this jersey, but seeing the Oilers embrace the color of oil (black) and then add a couple of fan-friendly touches to it to go along with the great logo, this jersey goes sneaky hard.

The Oilers Hometown Remix design gives it a kind of neon sign appearance by accident, and with the orange and blue stripes being a bit of a darker shade, they don't pop loudly, and that works with this. The shoulder logos featuring the oil driller shoulder logo used in the late 90s/early 2000s, along with a newer "Oil Country" circular logo featuring an oil derrick, are new and fun.

The eerie callback this jersey initially gave to their muted dark blue alternates from recent years made us worry about the similarity, but this one is discernibly different, and the new (and old) touches make it a really nice look.

Of all the Hometown Remix jerseys, this one might seem like old news, given it was one of the first ones to be leaked months ago. Fortunately, that leak didn't lead to any drastic changes because the Panthers leaning into the Miami Beach vibes means it's going to be a winner.

The jazzed-up former shoulder logo with the crossed palm tree and hockey stick, with a sunset behind it and the hem stripes playing out like a sunset, is fantastic. The sleeves coming off like their original jerseys in the design are great, as is the golden version of the Panthers logo on the sleeves.

A team wearing a pink jersey might be a bold call, but for a team out of South Florida wearing it? That's perfect. It even has us thinking about Grand Theft Auto 6 coming out for some reason...

We sort of got our wish for a new Kings jersey. We were looking for something new in purple and gold, and yes, L.A.'s Hometown Remix has that, but it's got a funky mix of black in there as well. As jarring as it may look up front, this jersey might cook on ice.

The purple jersey has a blacked-out Kings logo surrounded by gold, with gold, white, and black sleeve stripes. Within the sleeves are palm tree designs debossed within them, and the textural touches to the crown in the Kings logo and other bits of whimsy make it a real get-your-hands-on-it kind of jersey to appreciate.

The color balance is striking and not like anything we've really seen before, and that's not always a bad thing. We're eager to see this one in action all the same, to see how it really hits us. For now, we dig it for trying to be different.

We love our hockey fans in Minnesota, and we love them because they care so much for the Wild and what they used to have in the North Stars. The Wild's Hometown Remix brings back the colors of the Norm Green era of the North Stars and reclaims them for themselves.

We like how the black, green, and white colors play out here with the Wild logo (featuring a crescent moon), the stripes, and the addition of starlight spots in the numbers on the jersey; it's fun. What's even better are the debossed constellation star charts in the sleeves.

This jersey is meant to represent being in the wilderness at night and it nails that entire idea. It's another of the Remix jerseys that looks plain at first blush but when you dig into it, it's doing a lot of great things.

The problem with creating something new for the Montréal Canadiens is that you're doing something different than their already perfect jerseys. That's really tough.

What the Canadiens' Hometown Remix jersey was going to do was always going to fall short of what they've already got, but they've opted to lean hard into imagery and designs that play into the city itself.

The washed-out Canadiens logo on the front features designs meant to evoke the city's architecture, and the red gradient on the sides is meant to represent Mount Royal.

The symbols on the sleeves may make you wonder what in the world is going on there, but they're the symbols contained within the crest of the City of Montréal. These touches are nerdy, neat, and a lot of fun, but we're not sure any of this is at all coherently done.

Ooh-wee baby, this here is some honky-tonk.

This might be the most classically country music sports jersey ever made, and we're kind of into it. It's got a dark denim blue color, and the design choices on the front, shoulders, sleeves, and cuffs smack of something you'd see someone at the Grand Ole Opry wearing.

The Predators logo on the front has details within it that pay homage to classic country music stage designs, and the flowers on the sleeves are irises, the state flower of Tennessee. The numbers on the sleeves and back of the jersey will add even more country flavor to this design as well, and we love that.

These jerseys are meant to be representative of the hometowns and their history. The Preds crushed it in doing that with these.

The good thing about the Devils' Hometown Remix jersey is that it made sure to keep the "NJ" logo with the devil's tail prominently featured. The design of the logo gives it a raised edge around the logo that has a distinctly bold look and feel all the same.

The sleeves are simple, with some wavy design etched into them, but it's hard not to feel like we've seen these before from the Stadium Series in 2024, but color-swapped. That said, a blackout Devils jersey is something new and different for them, and this style is going to look slick on the ice.

The fisherman is back and bolder than ever. So are the lighter colors of an era many Islanders fans would like to forget when it comes to logos, jerseys and probably management, too.

The wavy hems are a throwback to the original Islanders fisherman jerseys, as are the lighthouse logos on the shoulders. If anything, these are a more tolerable version of the "fish sticks" jerseys from the 90s that were reviled by Isles fans and mocked by others.

But time heals, doesn't it? After all, the Fisherman logo's reputation was healed with time and seeing fans decked out in the old jerseys at games. Seeing it back and done (mostly) anew is fun, and considering how dull their Reverse Retro jerseys were, as well as their Stadium Series sweater, seeing this iteration of the Fisherman back is oddly heartwarming. We're positive, however, that Isles fans will have a lot to say about that.

We know it can be tough to be an Original Six team and to do something different, but the Rangers tried to put a touch of everything into their Hometown Remix.

The dark blue jersey is something we've seen from them in the recent past with their Heritage jersey from 2010 to 2017. Spelling out "New York" diagonally in the Rangers' drop-shadowed font was something we saw with their 9/11 tribute jerseys back on Oct. 7, 2001. The "Lady Liberty" logo high up on the chest came from their alternate jerseys from the 90s and 2000s.

The red stripes on the sleeves have the design from the torch of the Statue of Liberty debossed in them, which is something new and a cool touch. But even with all of these throwback design nods, it feels like well-worn territory for a Rangers sweater, and that's too bad.

We don't often think of the color gold being associated with the Ottawa Senators, but we will now, thanks to the Hometown Remix jersey.

The jersey is essentially a blacked-out and gold version of their home jersey. Any white that exists in the home sweater is wiped out, and gold takes over as the main highlight.

There are architectural designs tied to the City of Ottawa within the black sleeve stripes, and it's almost unfortunate that so much of this jersey is so dark because touches like that get lost. Even with all that gold, it's not enough to bring attention to them. It's a nice jersey, but it feels like there could've been more to be had here apart from gilding up the designs.

The Flyers' Hometown Remix is a classic example of "I see what you're aiming for, I'm just not totally sold on it."

Yes, the jersey is gray, but it's "Liberty Gray," as in the Liberty Bell, whose home is in downtown Philadelphia and serves as a symbol not just of America, but of everything in Philly itself. Gray is a tough color to work in hockey, and even with the Flyers having black and orange there to support it, as a jersey, it doesn't feel totally right.

Now there are other touches that make it work better. The orange numbers will have a "crack" in them as a further nod to the Liberty Bell, and that's fun. The striping on the sleeves is meant to echo the design of the Liberty Bell as well, and the inscription on the Liberty Bell is debossed in the sleeve stripes as well.

Maybe this one will grow on us over time, but for right now, the look isn't quite ringing for us.

The description given for the Penguins Hometown Remix makes note of its "pop art" touches, and doing something to pay homage to Andy Warhol and tying it to hockey would undoubtedly be seen as risky.

Not this time, though. This jersey absolutely rocks.

The Pens logo getting the Warhol treatment is meant to make you adjust your eyes and view it through a different kind of lens. The colors are all reminiscent of the Penguins' past, particularly the early years with the dark and light blues. There's gold weaving its way through it, and the triangular igloo logo that appears on their gold alternate jerseys is back on the shoulders of the Remix.

This jersey is a treat, and the numbers on the back get the same Warhol treatment as well, which gives it a kind of showtime dazzle. Jerseys aren't art, but this one comes really close to it.

What's the most popular part of a shark? Sure, it might be the dorsal fin, but sharks' teeth are in the running, and they figure prominently on the San Jose Sharks Hometown Remix jersey.

The sleeves on the light teal jersey show off the razor-sharp teeth of a shark, gums and all, that flow into blackness from the elbows down. The body of the jersey has a bold "SJ" with a shark roaring around it for the crest, a mostly new design that would look great on a hat, while a shark head logo rests on the shoulders.

This is a bright and fun jersey, which is what Sharks hockey is meant to be, and we like that.

The Kraken have a great primary logo, but they also introduced a great secondary logo when they began playing years ago with the ship anchor that has the Space Needle woven into the design.

Using that logo for a jersey was something we hoped to see one day, and now that time is here.

The Kraken's Hometown Remix goes hard with the navy-blue jersey and the anchor/Space Needle logo, while the main logo sits on the shoulders. While the team colors are very much in play on this jersey, it also makes us think a bit of the Seattle Mariners as well with the design, and that's not a bad thing.

The numbers and Kraken logo on the shoulder, as well as the main logo, have designs in them meant to evoke scrimshaw design, a style used for art and maps centuries ago. What a deep pull! This jersey is incredible, and the Kraken keep killing it with their styles.

The Blues busted out a kind of redesign of a former third-jersey logo to be the centerpiece of their Hometown Remix.

The circular logo featuring the classic Blue Note logo as well as the St. Louis Arch is similar to one that adorned their alternate jerseys from 2008 to 2016. The one change to it is three wavy lines added on each side of the circle, meant to represent the Mississippi River that borders the city.

A black jersey with blue stripes and silver outlines was a bit unexpected. The sleeves have a debossed wavy pattern to lean into the Mighty Mississippi's presence again. While a black jersey can be interesting, this jersey falls short despite all of the local nods.

One of the parts of the Lightning's Stadium Series jersey we really liked was the circular skull logo with a lightning-shaped crack in it, and we've been rewarded with it taking the spot as the primary crest of their Hometown Remix jersey.

With such an obvious nod to Gasparilla and the city's attachment to pirates, getting that logo back in a bigger way is a lot of fun. While that's got a loose attachment to actual lightning, fear not; the lightning-shaped sleeve stripes fill that need.

It's a black jersey with sky-blue logos and stripes, and that's always a happy combination of colors. While this one might seem subdued because of the coloring, it's a great jersey nonetheless.

The beauty of being called the Maple Leafs is that you can style up an actual leaf from a maple tree and go to town, and that's just what Toronto has done.

The blue, old-timey-looking leaf on the front, with "TORONTO" in an old-style font underneath it on a cream-white jersey, evokes the past and a classic feel but is entirely something new. The striped sleeves are fascinating given that they're blue and white, but not the same shade of white as the jersey. It's eye-catching in an odd way, but it's a way to make sure you don't mistake this jersey for being something meant for a Heritage or Winter Classic.

This gear will assuredly be a hit with older fans, but seeing Auston Matthews and Gavin McKenna ripping around the ice in them should be enough to make everyone want to add these to their collection.

We've been anxious for when the Utah Mammoth would add a baby blue third jersey ever since they unveiled their color scheme as a franchise, and their Hometown Remix jersey grants our wish.

Given that the Mammoth doesn't have much of a history to work with, the world was their oyster for how to draw this one up, and while they didn't mail it in, they didn't stretch their legs out too much either.

The Mammoth used one of their secondary logos for the crest, and the tusked-out "U" is a cool logo, and the looping tusk-shaped stripes on the shoulders, waist, and sleeves are also cool. The Mammoth logo on the shoulders checks out, but this feels like it could just be a regular alternate jersey...which could be in the future if it winds up being popular.

But for this project, we like when teams push boundaries and this one feels very safely done, which is understandable.

Another black jersey with dark blue as the primary color comes through here for Vancouver, and, man, this is a let-down.

Given everything wild we've seen from Vancouver for the alternates, Reverse Retros, and all throughout the franchise's history, getting this for the Hometown Remix is deflating.

The theme for this one is "Vancouver at Night" and while the blacked-out orca in the crest logo is cool, especially with the glowing eye, all of the debossed designs of the city skyline and bay in the sleeves still can't win us over. We could've had more Johnny Canuck or the V's or even more of the "Flying Skate" and instead we just get the Canucks with the lights off. Bummer.

You might say you're going to Las Vegas for the shows or to watch the Golden Knights, but we know for sure you're stopping by a casino somehow, and the tables will call to you. Vegas' Hometown Remix makes us want to heed that call and play our favorite number on the roulette wheel.

The felt green stripes and shoulder yoke with the black base for the jersey scream "casino night," and if that didn't do it, the red and black design on the sleeves will tell you what's up. The gold outline on the logo and sleeves gives it more of the Vegas touch, as does the debossed "Vegas" sign style within the sleeves.

Vegas leaning into being in Las Vegas for their designs is always a winner and this jersey fits right into that.

The Capitals Hometown Remix jersey answers the question of "What if you took their old alternate logo and put it on the blue screaming eagle jersey instead?" That's assuredly a very real question that's been asked, and now it's been answered with a great response.

The Caps' U.S. Capitol logo from the 1990s/2000s gets the primary treatment on a jersey that's reminiscent of their current red alternate, only it's the same teal-blue color the Capitals used during the '90s instead.

This jersey is great to look at, and the color scheme from back in the day was a very good one. Seeing it again in this style of jersey, with the screaming eagles on the shoulders, is a nostalgia party while being something very new yet still familiar.

The white, gold and black stripes are done in a way that's unique and the numbers are designed in a way similar to the monuments around D.C. with marble texturing and everything. Phenomenal work.

If you've never seen the Aurora Borealis, you can get an idea of what it's like with the Winnipeg Jets Hometown Remix sweater.

It's a wonder to see a jersey weave the wispy colors of the aurora into sleeve striping to give it the look of the Northern Lights on fabric. The way that same color effect is woven into the Jets logos on the crest and shoulders, with the nighttime sky background of the jersey, is really fun.

Getting this kind of an artistic take with a jersey and to use the Aurora Borealis as the subject is inspired stuff and we love that.

articles.title: Sami Zayn is Right, WWE's Huge Gamble, John Cena Classic Woes and More Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York hosted the November 2 edition of Raw on Netflix, building the final hype for Crown Jewel.
articles.body:
The Barclays Center in Brooklyn, New York hosted the November 2 edition of WWE Raw on Netflix, building the final hype for Crown Jewel.

The 946 and Sami Zayn got one up on Roman Reigns and The Bloodline as the heel stable added NXT's Cruz Montana and set up the undisputed WWE champion to lay out The OTC to end the night.

"All Ego" Ethan Page captured the Intercontinental Championship from Chad Gable, while John Cena gave WWE fans more details about the new Cena Classic.

It was an important go-home show for the red brand that left fans with much to consider for Saturday's premium live event in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.

Sami Zayn is Right. But It Doesn't Matter

Sami Zayn continues to deliver some of the best promos in WWE each week, but as the established heel, crowds do not care to give him any recognition.

The Last Real Good Guy clearly highlighted the flaws in Roman Reigns' game and history while showcasing his own consistency in an underrated role.

His speech made a clear point. Zayn deserves to beat The OTC at Crown Jewel and establish himself as the top world champion in WWE for the next year.

It won't happen though for one simple reason: Reigns is the bigger star.

He barely has to say anything to "win" every argument, and crowds accept that he should win against anyone.

Zayn is not going to be treated as a bigger deal than Reigns at any point in his career, no matter what both men do.

The Biggest Test of Ethan Page's Career Begins

The new Intercontinental champion "All Ego" Ethan Page made strong impression from his initial Raw debut, and he has not disappointed with any opportunity.

He is a great in-ring worker and an even better talker that has sold himself as the problem heel no one wants to deal with.

As the champion, All Ego is perfectly positioned to take a lead role for the red brand that can establish his long-term potential.

If he continues to deliver against bigger competition, Page could be soon taking lead roles at premium live events, eventually challenging for either of the world titles.

If the run does not go well, it is unlikely Page will lose all value, but it is unlikely he will get any chances to truly challenge the top names in WWE.

All signs pointed to Page succeeding, but nothing is certain yet. Hopefully Page can make the most of his spotlight.

John Cena is Failing to Sell the John Cena Classic

What is The John Cena Classic? According to The GOAT himself, it will be the second Raw on December 14 where WWE and NXT Superstars will fight for the vote of Club WWE Members.

The Superstar fans vote to win will be awarded a special championship.

When Cena first introduced this concept, it sounded like he was confident in this to be a premium live event, but it looks to be a mere TV special and one that could be eclipsed by a different Raw earlier in the day.

The GOAT's enthusiasm for highlighting NXT stars is infectious, but if this was just about showcasing the developmental stars, there is no reason for this vote and championship.

No NXT star is going to win out on a vote over the established talent of Raw and SmackDown, even with a limited audience that needs to pay for the right to vote.

Instead, the whole concept has quickly evolved into a Club WWE advertisement that is unlikely to improve fan interest in the subscription service.

If The GOAT cannot sell this idea to fans, who can? This will quickly become a one-and-done for WWE unless the company makes drastic changes after year one.

The Crown Jewel Gimmick Needs to Be Scrapped

Much like the John Cena Classic Championship, the Crown Jewel Championshisp are a once-a-year title that never matters except on the night of the PLE.

Perhaps a more apt comparison is the forgotten Great Royal Rumble Championship, which was also a title that was never seen again after the night of the Greatest Royal Rumble.

In all of these cases, fans do not care about a title that is not regularly presented on television.

Why should fans care if Liv Morgan or Chelsea Green are the Crown Jewel champion when it has not impact on either of their actual championship reigns?

Seth Rollins won the 2025 men's Crown Jewel Championship over Cody Rhodes, and he is not even in the conversation around the PLE this year.

Liv has a chance to become a two-time Crown Jewel champion, an accolade that would only be referenced again on the road to future Crown Jewel events.

Liv vs. Green is more important to the product as a potential vehicle to a Tiffany Stratton Money in the Bank cash-in, and Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn is a speed bump in The OTC's feud with 946.

Why distract from the main stories WWE wants to tell in order to award a championship that will not be showcased at all on weekly TV?

It is time to retire this concept and just return Crown Jewel to the status of standard PLE where top champions defend their actual gold.

Cruz Montana was a major signing for NXT in July from TNA, looking like a major threat in the NXT Championship scene.

He was set up as the most likely man to dethrone Grayson Waller as NXT champion, once he put DarkState behind him possibly as early as this Wednesday in an Unsanctioned match against Dion Lennox.

Instead, it looks like this week's NXT could be the last performance from Montana as he has joined 946 in the fight against The Bloodline on Raw.

This is a huge spotlight on a 35-year-old veteran whose long term WWE future was uncertain until this moment.

Montana has history in the business going back to 2007, including time in All Elite Wrestling and two TNA World Championship reigns.

As a late arrival in WWE, he could have been type-cast as a veteran on track to become a coach. Instead, as a member of 946, he is likely to main event Survivor Series: WarGames.

While Royce Keys remains 946's leader for now, WWE has set up three singles star that could break out in Keys, Carmelo Hayes and Montana.

There is a chance that this surprise Raw debut is a harbinger of a big run to come for The Real Deal.

articles.title: Making the Case For an LA Knight Heel Turn on WWE Raw
articles.summary: The LA Knight heel turn, when WWE pulls the trigger, will reshape the main event landscape.
articles.body:
The LA Knight heel turn, when WWE pulls the trigger, will reshape the main event landscape.

Call it a when conversation now, not an if . All that stands in the way of a Knight turn is proper timing in that main event scene, so it can be pulled off to its full potential.

Right now, one could argue WWE has fans right where it wants them with Knight. He just dropped another title bout with Roman Reigns, this time at Money in the Bank. He's the lovable loser in that Dolph Ziggler role who can't win the big one. He's even got a modern splash of behind-the-scenes pity due to those documentary-like appearances where Triple H and others are just down on him.

Feel free to call it wishful thinking. But it takes one flip of the switch to capitalize on all this midness and turn it into greatness.

Because that's where we're at with Knight. He's still generating massive crowd reactions. The payoff is still banked. This isn't a case of needing the perfect window that has an expiration date. He's not cooling off, which, for better or worse, makes him quite the asset for WWE.

All of this is fuel, too. Knight is "old," he "botches," Oba Femi, Bron Breakker and Penta have passed him by. His chances of winning are so slim that WWE throws his big championship match out as the opener just to get the crowd worked up at Money in the Bank. It goes on and on. Now he's back in tag/stable purgatory.

It's all fuel. Knight can twist these things to his advantage in his character work, railing against corporate overlords who hold him back. Everyone knows he has the look and a violent streak that can create violent heel moments.

Everyone else's gain can be Knight's, too. It's not like he's going to stop moving merchandise or being super-over with live crowds because he goes heel. He might even sell more merchandise and draw bigger reactions.

And if we're talking about sales concerns? The little kids who don't want to buy his merch anymore still have Jey Uso, Femi and a bunch of others. There's room for a guy like Knight to shift and do more interesting things than be a 2000s catchphrase emulator.

Look at the upcoming slate for possible examples. Maybe Knight's big heel moment is helping The 946 take down The Bloodline at Survivor Series. That keeps Roman Reigns looking strong and could let Knight fully break free on his own solo run.

Maybe there's an angle up for grabs with the Money in the Bank contract. If Penta cools, the company could always throw out a curveball, like Knight finding a way to "win" or "steal" the briefcase before cashing it in.

Sound silly? Easy to forget this is pro wrestling. There's always a way out of a corner or a way to unlock new things. No need to overthink Knight's character finally snapping and doing pretty much whatever he wants. He can even loop in meta things for his rampage, such as threatening to leave for other wrestling promotions, too.

Not to wax too poetic, but Knight could really be a good example or a bridge between the faker characters of the past and modern "Superstars" who just want to be great and break kayfabe on their Instagram accounts.

The Megastar is sort of torn between two times, and it would be fun for fans to explore these themes and go along for the ride with him.

Again, it's almost to his detriment at times, but Knight's love from fans isn't fading. That gives all involved some leeway to pick and choose the right spot. But it's not indefinite, and fans can only watch a beloved wrestler miss the brass ring so many times before moving on to something else.

articles.title: Report Card Grades for Every NHL Team's First Month of the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The first month of the NHL season can start to tell you a lot about where a team is and where its season might be going.
articles.body:
The first month of the NHL season can start to tell you a lot about where a team is and where its season might be going.

It is not too soon to start worrying for some teams that are off to disappointing or slow starts, and it is not too soon to start raising expectations for teams off to strong starts.

American Thanksgiving is usually one of the big cut-off lines for which teams make the playoffs and which ones do not, and that is only a few weeks away at this point.

So now that we are starting to get closer to that, it's time to hand out some updated grades and issue our next report card for the 2026-27 season.

Grades are simply based on what we have seen so far in the first month. There is still time for teams to turn things around (or get worse).

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

The big question for the Ducks this season was whether or not they had enough defense to take another step forward after making the playoffs in 2025-26.

The early returns: Still some work to do.

They are 29th in the NHL in expected goals against per 60 minutes during 5-on-5 play and, unlike last year, are not yet outscoring all of their defensive issues. They are outscoring some of them, but not all of them.

They spent most of their summer dealing with their own restricted free agents, probably spending way more than they intended, and never had a chance to fix their biggest weakness (the defense).

The good news? The young forwards (Leo Carlsson, Beckett Sennecke and Cutter Gauthier) are absolutely rolling.

There should have been some legitimate concerns about this team's ceiling entering the season, given how much of their 2025-26 success was tied to goaltending and how weak their defensive metrics were.

But through the first month, the Bruins have one of the best records in the league, and even though some of their defensive metrics are still lagging a little, they are generating a lot more offensively to at least keep them above water in terms of out-chancing their opponents.

It's not all falling on goaltender Jeremy Swayman.

The infusion of young talent with players like Fraser Minten and James Hagens has been a breath of fresh air and is giving this team some much-needed spark.

For the first time in more than 15 years, the Buffalo Sabres entered a season with major expectations.

There were some questions about what that ceiling could be after an offseason that mostly saw them subtract instead of add. But if there was a team that seemed capable of overcoming that, the Sabres were it, given the young talent on the roster that was coming back (not to mention stars like Tage Thompson and Rasmus Dahlin).

For the most part, things are going well, but you do have to wonder if maybe they missed a big opportunity to take a big swing at upgrading their goalie position by missing out on Connor Hellebuyck.

That would have given everyone—from the fans to the players—a shot in the arm.

Are the goalies going to be good enough over a full season? It's a valid question.

The only expectation for the Flames this season was that they would lose, and lose a lot. This is one of the few rosters in the NHL that looks to be in a full-scale rebuild, and it is short on talent in most areas.

So far, they are at least putting up a fight and hanging in some games ... and winning some.

Goalie Devin Cooley has played a big part in that early success.

It's still a team that is likely to fade as the season goes on, but they are not yet the complete disaster they were supposed to be. The lack of offense will eventually be the killer here.

The defending Stanley Cup champions have looked exactly like you would expect them to look.

Grinding teams down, owning the puck, setting up shop in the offensive zone, and getting just enough goaltending behind all of that to keep winning games. And even that undersells the goaltending, where Pyotr Kochetkov has been outstanding to open the season.

It is, again, a team that has no real weaknesses. The star power that most champions have is not quite there in big-name appeal, but you won't get a shift off against anybody here.

What is truly scary about them is that they have the trade assets and salary cap space to make a big splash and add to that at some point this season. They are still great. They can easily make themselves better. A lot better.

The front office apologists, and probably the front office itself, will tell you that Connor Bedard's absence at the start of the season played a big role in the slow start.

But it should not have resulted in them being completely uncompetitive. Even after his return, they still aren't anywhere close to being a competitive team.

Everybody loves the young talent on paper.

But not all of these guys are going to succeed given the attrition rate of prospects, and there is also the question of how well these guys will develop by getting steamrolled every single night in the NHL.

Losing breeds more losing. This team is still losing a lot.

It's not a bad start by any means, and the offense led by Nathan MacKinnon is as dominant as ever. But they have only been a middle-of-the-pack team defensively and in terms of driving possession.

There's still time for those areas to correct themselves.

It's also a veteran team that knows it's going to be a playoff team and probably hasn't flipped the switch just yet. Let's see how they look around February. It will probably look a lot different (and better) than this.

Head coach Rick Bowness is still trying to change the culture here, and it's still an uphill battle. It's also a very subjective thing to work on and address, and the only way to fix it is by winning more hockey games. How do they do that? From a more tangible and objective perspective, the biggest issue so far is the lack of offense. Kent Johnson is having a nice start to the season, but a lot of returning veterans are really struggling to make an impact.

Entering play on Monday, Zach Werenski, Charlie Coyle, Valeri Nichushkin, Sean Monahan, and Matthew Knies had combined for just five goals in the first 12 games.

That is not good enough. They need more from some of those players.

Solid. Really solid. The underlying numbers are painting a strong picture in terms of the Stars' ability to push play. Jason Robertson and Mikko Rantanen are off to great starts offensively, and perhaps the most encouraging sign of them all is the dominant start from No. 1 goalie Jake Oettinger.

When he is on his game, there are few goalies in the NHL better than him.

He entered the week plus 9.8 in goals saved above expected, which is the second-highest mark in the league. If you get goaltending like that, you are always going to have a chance, no matter what the rest of your team looks like. When a good team is getting goaltending like that, you are going to be a serious Stanley Cup contender.

There are two different layers of the Red Wings right now.

The front office and ownership deserve an F for their hockey decisions over the past year—and, frankly, for longer than that.

And then there is the situation with the players actually on the ice and the way they are playing. So far? You have to give them some credit for being as competitive as they have been, given the three-ring circus going on around them. It would have been easy for everybody here to just mentally and emotionally check out.

They are a top-10 team in expected goal share.

There are some good individual performances here.

Am I grading on a curve, given everything else happening with the organization? Maybe. But there is a solid process in place with the way the team is actually playing, and they are shutting out a lot of noise to play some really good hockey. That is worth something.

The record speaks for itself. They are off to one of the best starts in franchise history, and the superstar trio of Connor McDavid, Leon Draisaitl, and Evan Bouchard is the driving force behind it.

McDavid is playing some of the best individual hockey we have seen from a player in decades, and he looks like he might challenge the league's single-season point record.

Bouchard is doing what he normally does, and finally getting some recognition for it. He is playing at a Norris Trophy level.

The only two things that keep this as an A-minus instead of an A are…

They have not really been tested with the schedule just yet.

And they are still a really bad team when McDavid and Draisaitl are off the ice. Entering play on Monday, Edmonton had been outscored 20–12 at five-on-five with neither player on the ice, with a 37 percent expected goal share.

That depth needs to get better. It simply does. It is working now in October against a lot of pretenders and lottery teams. They need it to work in April, May, and June against real contenders.

They are mostly beating the teams they should beat, and they are doing it without top center Aleksander Barkov. Unlike last year, they at least know he will be back at some point this season. And when he is back, that should again put them back among the league's top contenders.

The Tkachuk brothers are off to great starts, but one of the bigger developments is defenseman Seth Jones playing some of the best hockey of his career. He has been really good since joining the Panthers, but he looks outstanding so far this season.

Once again, there is simply not enough offense and not enough difference-makers here. They are still waiting for Quinton Byfield to take a big step, and outside of Artemi Panarin, nobody has really generated much in the way of scoring to move the needle.

Even worse: A lot of the territorial and defensive dominance they have shown over the past few years is not quite here this season. They are a bottom-10 team in expected goal share and are not really pushing play the way we have seen in the past. That needs to be better. A lot of things need to be better, but it's hard to imagine where it is going to come from.

This roster has shown us what it is -- a middle-of-the-road team that will compete for a playoff spot, probably get there, and not do much else when it does.

The stars are shining brightly in Minnesota.

Kirill Kaprizov is averaging a goal per game, Quinn Hughes is playing sensational hockey, and Jesper Wallstedt has been the best goalie in the league so far.

But there are some big questions lurking under the surface.

What is general manager Bill Guerin going to do with Hughes if he can not get him signed beyond this season?

Will they find a way to get another center to help fill one of the biggest holes on the roster?

Related to the second question, do they have enough assets to entice the Red Wings to trade them, Dylan Larkin?

If they keep Hughes all season and add a center, there is reason to believe here.

But neither of those things is a given right now.

After losing three of their first four games, the Canadiens have gone on a roll, and the most impressive part of that is the fact that they have done it without No. 1 center Nick Suzuki.

That is especially impressive because center depth was the one big question on this team, even with Suzuki in the lineup. Seeing the team still win games without him has to be an encouraging development for the front office and coaching staff.

Goalie Jacob Fowler deserves a lot of the credit for that, as he has been one of the best goalies in the league through the first month of the season. That is another encouraging development.

You could say the Predators are playing up to expectations, and that is kind of the problem from a big-picture perspective.

They're just kind of stuck in the middle of the league.

In a vacuum, a lot of their offseason moves were solid additions, but there wasn't anybody who was going to change the outlook. The core players are older and past their prime, and while the farm system is strong and has a lot of players that could be very solid NHL regulars, there probably is not a franchise-changing superstar in it.

It's an average team that will have a chance to make the playoffs, but probably won't do much more than that.

That is pretty much how the first month has played out.

It might be time to start paying attention to the Devils as a potential contender. Perhaps as soon as this season.

They have an outstanding 1-2 center duo in Jack Hughes and Nico Hischier; they addressed a lot of their depth issues over the summer. They have some of the best possession and scoring-chance metrics in the league (second in the entire NHL in expected goal share during 5-on-5 play), and now they have one of the best goalies in the NHL in Connor Hellebuyck.

More importantly, why isn't that a contender?

Just imagine them next season with Quinn Hughes in that lineup. It could happen.

It's not a great roster from top to bottom, but any roster that has an emerging superstar defenseman (Matthew Schaefer) and one of the best goalies in the NHL (Ilya Sorokin) is going to have a shot in the playoff race.

It's going to take a lot of heavy lifting from those two guys, but if you are going to lean heavily on one or two players to carry you, a franchise goalie and No. 1 defenseman that can take over any game, on any night, is a good place to start.

The lack of goal-scoring is (and is going to be) the concern, but they will win their share of games.

Absolutely brutal luck for the Rangers when it comes to the season-ending Igor Shesterkin injury. If he were healthy, this could have easily been a playoff team, given a lot of the improvements they made over the summer.

They are a middle-of-the-pack team in expected goals (which is actually a big jump from the past five or six years), have a healthy Adam Fox, are getting a breakout season from Alexis Lafreniere, and have improved some of the depth pieces on their defense.

It should be, at the very least, a respectable complementary cast for a franchise goalie.

And then Shesterkin was lost for the season in his fifth start.

Dylan Garand is doing everything he can and is at least giving them some league-average goaltending, but he's not going to steal many games or be a difference-maker the way Shesterkin is.

Brady Tkachuk is an outstanding player, but losing him was never going to completely take them out of the playoff picture.

They are showing there is still a really good team in place here, and that is especially true with starting goalie Linus Ullmark playing well. They could certainly use an upgrade behind him at the backup spot, but he is back to playing at an elite level when healthy.

What makes their start even more impressive is the injuries they have had to play through. Not only has Ullmark missed time, but Jake Sanderson, Thomas Chabot and Artem Zub (three of their top defensemen) have combined to miss 19 man-games due to injury, while forward William Eklund, acquired in the offseason using one of the draft picks received in the Tkachuk trade, has been limited to just four games.

It's a good defensive team; it still has a star forward in Tim Stützle, and if Ullmark stays healthy and plays well, it also has a top-level starting goalie.

They can absolutely make the playoffs again. If they do, they will not be an easy out.

The best development here so far is the fact that Matvei Michkov has 10 goals in 16 games.

The concern with that is the fact that he is carrying a 43.5 percent shooting percentage, and that number is going to regress significantly in the coming weeks and months.

Beyond that? There is not much to be overly positive about here.

The Flyers were always a strong candidate to regress this season, but it's kind of shocking just how much they have regressed over the first month.

There is almost no offense; they have taken a step backward defensively, and they have just four wins in 16 games despite still getting solid goaltending (Joseph Woll and Dan Vladar are a combined 3.5 goals saved above expected).

Their entire offseason plan seemed to revolve around getting that Leo Carlsson offer sheet to work in their favor, and when it did not, they did not seem to have any sort of a Plan B.

They can score goals, but they are an absolute mess defensively at times, and the goaltending duo of Artūrs Šilovs and Sergei Murashov has been wildly inconsistent. Murashov is the future and an exciting prospect, but he is definitely playing through some growing pains early on.

Beyond that, one of the biggest issues here has been the play of the top line that is centered by Sidney Crosby. They played their best game of the season on Saturday night, but prior to that, it was, by every objective measure, their worst-performing line of the season.

The Penguins are rebuilding, even if it is not a complete teardown, but they still have a chance to contend for a playoff spot again. But if that is going to happen, they are going to need more consistency from their defense and goaltending, and they are going to need a lot more from Crosby and the top line.

The two things keeping the Sharks afloat right now are Macklin Celebrini and some shockingly strong goaltending.

Celebrini has 16 points in 14 games, while Yaroslav Askarov and Alex Nedeljkovic have a combined 10.9 goals saved above expected in net.

The problem is they are getting outscored 12-24 during 5-on-5 play when Celebrini is off the ice, while they are only 29th in the NHL in expected goal share.

There is a really encouraging core of young talent at forward, but the rest of the roster is still mostly terrible, especially on defense. It is a team that is still a long, long way from contention, even with one of the game's best players and some exciting young players starting to make their way into the league.

The Kraken are exceeding expectations so far, but there is good reason to be skeptical of how sustainable it is over the course of the season.

Their goaltending has been below average; they are near the bottom of the league in expected goal share, and most of their success is coming from an offense that is being carried by a 14.2 percent shooting percentage. It's helped them stack some points early on and build a little bit of a cushion for when the regression to the mean offensively eventually hits, but they are going to need an even bigger cushion to help make up for the inevitable slide offensively.

Turning the net over to Joel Hofer instead of Jordan Binnington is the smart decision, and it's giving the Blues a chance to compete this season.

Even after trading Jordan Kyrou this offseason, there is a solid forward group here that is just starting to reach its prime years, and a few of them are off to slow starts that should turn around at some point. When they do, and assuming they keep giving Hofer the net, this could be an interesting team in the Western Conference.

They still need some help on the back end, but the group of forwards featuring Robert Thomas, Jake Neighbours, Jimmy Snuggerud, Dylan Holloway, Mason McTavish and Connor McMichael is intriguing. There isn't really a star in that group, but when Thomas is at his best, he is one of the most underrated players in the league.

Mediocre start for the team, but there is a decent ceiling here.

Their season has been thrown into some unexpected chaos with the Nikita Kucherov trade request, and that's a shame for them because this is still a team that should have a window for contention that is cracked open this season.

Their core is getting older, and they have not had much playoff success in recent years, but they still play a winning brand of hockey and still have a championship-worthy core.

They are fourth in the league in expected goal share and their top stars (Kucherov, Brandon Hagel and Jake Guentzel) are all playing great.

The one thing that is holding them back? Goaltending. Andrei Vasilevskiy has not really played his best hockey to date. Given his age and the number of games and minutes he has played over the years, there is going to come a point where he does start to slow down, but he probably isn't there quite yet. If he gets back on track, this team can cause some problems. Especially if they keep Kucherov.

Auston Matthews looks like he is back to being elite.

William Nylander is still playing like a star.

Gavin McKenna's rookie season is off to a strong start.

Those are all huge developments for the Maple Leafs, but they still have some big flaws in their defensive play and a big question in goal with Sergei Bobrovsky. Bobrovsky was one of the Maple Leafs' biggest offseason additions, and the hope was that he could rediscover some of his past glory and show that he still has something left in the tank.

So far, he has not done anything to justify the Maple Leafs' confidence in him.

It probably should have been a potential red flag when one of the best-run teams in the league (Florida) decided to part ways with a late-30s goalie coming off one of the worst seasons of his career.

Utah is one of the teams in the league where the record (9-6-0 entering play on Tuesday) does not really match the level of play.

It should be better, and they have played well enough for it to be better.

This team is good. Really good. They are fast, aggressive, and relentless on the forecheck, have one of the league's most dominant power play units through the first month, and have pieced together a really good young core of talent, complemented wonderfully by an aggressive front office that has kept adding around it.

Everything about this team's process just screams "contender."

They just might need one more thing to bring it all together.

Connor Hellebuyck could have been that one thing, and it might prove to be a missed opportunity for them.

It is tempting to give them an F for how bad they have been, but their being bad is pretty much what we all expected.

This is the worst roster in the league on paper, and it is very clear this rebuild is just getting underway and is going to take a very long time to complete.

The F's feel like they should be reserved for the bad teams that are somehow worse than expected.

As bad as this start has been for the Canucks, there is at least one positive this season: The play of center Elias Pettersson. After back-to-back down years that made it look like his days as a top-line scorer were over, Pettersson is off to a point-per-game start and is showing some of the skill and creativity that made him a 100-point scorer at one point in his career.

Whether it is to use him as a trade chip or to make sure they still have a top-line player for themselves, Pettersson's resurgence this season is a huge positive development.

The trio of Jack Eichel, Mark Stone, and Mitch Marner is setting the tone offensively, and the team as a whole is mostly carrying the play on any given night.

Imagine how good they could be if they had even above-average goaltending.

Finding a goalie upgrade is going to be tough, but you should still expect them to be active on the trade market. They always are. If Kucherov really does become available, do not rule them out because they always find a way to get a shiny new toy and a superstar player when they become available.

Where there is a will, there is a way. They will find it if the opportunity presents itself.

After a big offseason that saw them land Alex Tuch, Jordan Kyrou, and Boone Jenner, the expectations for the Capitals went through the roof.

In most normal years, they would have had enough points to make the playoffs a year ago, and they are not only bringing back most of that roster, but they have also improved on a lot of it.

Some of those improvements are paying off, specifically as it relates to Tuch with his 10 goals already.

But so far, something is missing here, and it might be some additional help on the blue line. They are going to score more goals, and Logan Thompson has not played his best hockey yet. But it is worth wondering if they have enough depth on their defense to hang with the biggest contenders in the NHL.

It is easy to really like their young players, specifically Ryan Leonard, Cole Hutson, and the Protas brothers (Aliaksei and Ilya), and it is easy to love a lot of the veterans they have coming back and have brought in. But another top-four defender would go a long way for them.

They are starting to see what the roster general manager, Kevin Cheveldayoff, has built is capable of when it does not have one of the best goalies in the world (Connor Hellebuyck) bailing it out every night. It is not good. Winnipeg has won just four of its first 15 games, enters Tuesday on a nine-game losing streak, and outside of Kyle Connor, Cole Perfetti and Mark Scheifele, there is not much to like about any aspect of this team's play this season.

Not having their top defenseman, Josh Morrissey, has certainly hurt, but for as good as he is, he is not going to fix all of this team's struggles. It is simply a poorly constructed team that does not seem to have any sort of plan or direction at the moment. This could be a very long season.

articles.title: Diego Molina y Blanca López dan a España sus primeras medallas en Dakar gracias al remo de mar
articles.summary: La delegación española en los Juegos Olímpicos de la Juventud de Dakar 2026 ha conseguido las primeras medallas gracias al remo de mar individual. Los deportistas laureados han sido Diego Molina y Blanca López.
articles.body: La delegación española en los Juegos Olímpicos de la Juventud de Dakar 2026 ha conseguido las primeras medallas gracias al remo de mar individual. Los deportistas laureados han sido Diego Molina y Blanca López. Diego Molina se hizo con la medalla de plata tras superar en cuartos de final al italiano Davide Gazzola y en semifinales al egipcio Youssuf Mourisi; en la final no pudo con el sudafricano Callum Dreyer. En féminas, Blanca López se impuso en cuartos a la austríaca Alena Lux en un enfrentamiento muy igualado pero en semifinales cedió ante la china Lili Liu, a la postre campeona. En la lucha por el bronce ganó a la checa Marie Zavadilova por 29 centésimas. Molina y López cayeron en cuartos de final del dobles mixto, pero en las pruebas individuales demostraron por qué España es una de las principales potencias de este deporte. Recordemos que el remo de mar, novedad en Dakar 2026, será uno de los nuevos deportes olímpicos de LA28.

articles.title: Nadal, a Carolina Marín: "Has hecho algo único"
articles.summary: El ídolo de Carolina Marín, desde sus inicios, ha sido Rafa Nadal. La campeona olímpica de bádminton siempre ha reconocido su admiración por él.  Una admiración que es mutua en la actualidad, por eso el ganador de 22 Grand Slams de tenis ha querido felicitarla con motivo del MARCA Leyenda.  "Un premio más que merecido", comienza diciendo. Y pone en valor "una carrera increíble en la que has hecho algo único, que es ser pionera en traer el bádminton a las pantallas de nuestro país con la dificultad que eso conlleva. Muchísimas felicidades y ya sabes que te tengo mucha admiración", reconoce.  Y acaba deseándole que sea muy feliz en esta nueva etapa tras su retirada. "Te deseo lo mejor para esta nueva etapa de tu vida, que seguro que va a ser preciosa. Un beso grande".

articles.title: Noruega, Dinamarca y Suecia se niegan a enfrentarse a Rusia en el Mundial de hockey sobre hielo
articles.standfirst: Pes a que el TAS dictaminó hace unos días el regreso de Rusia a las competiciones de hockey hielo
articles.summary: Pes a que el TAS dictaminó hace unos días el regreso de Rusia a las competiciones de hockey hielo
articles.body: Las federaciones de hockey sobre hielo de Noruega, Dinamarca y Suecia anunciaron este martes que no se enfrentarán a Rusia en el próximo Mundial masculino de Alemania, tras la reciente decisión del Tribunal de Arbitraje del Deporte (TAS) de permitir su regreso a las competiciones internacionales de ese deporte. El TAS había dado la razón el pasado día 30 a Rusia en su litigio con la Federación Internacional de Hockey sobre Hielo (IIHF, por sus siglas en inglés) al considerar que los motivos de seguridad alegados por ese organismo para excluir a las selecciones rusas "carecen de pruebas suficientes". Las tres federaciones apelaron a la guerra en Ucrania y a la seguridad de sus deportistas para negarse a jugar contra Rusia, aunque no boicotearán el campeonato. "Nuestra opinión es que Rusia debe ser excluida de todos los torneos internacionales mientras continúe la guerra en Ucrania. Nuestra decisión se basa también en la responsabilidad de cuidar la seguridad y el bienestar de nuestros jugadores, técnicos y sus familias", señaló en un comunicado la Federación noruega. El presidente de la Federación Danesa de Hockey, Henrik Bach Nielsen, declaró a la agencia Ritzau su negativa a enfrentarse a Rusia, decisión que ya ha comunicado a la IIHF. "Se trata de nuestra seguridad y la de todos nuestros colaboradores: jugadores, aficionados, patrocinadores. En consideración a la integridad del hockey no podemos enfrentarnos a Rusia ahora mismo", afirmó Nielsen. Noruega, Dinamarca y Suecia se unen así a Finlandia, que ya había anunciado la víspera su negativa a enfrentarse a la selección rusa. El Gobierno alemán abogó ayer por una política de visados restrictiva en el caso de deportistas rusos. El portavoz del Ejecutivo, Stefan Kornelius, mostró su "escepticismo" sobre la decisión del TAS y recordó que tanto la Federación Alemana de Hockey sobre Hielo (DEB), como la internacional, han anunciado que analizarán minuciosamente el dictamen y su argumentación. Agregó que el Gobierno debatirá en breve con la federación alemana las posibles consecuencias, también para el mundial masculino de 2027 en Alemania.

articles.title: Carolina Marín, el mito interminable, ya es MARCA Leyenda
articles.standfirst: MARCA condecora con su gran galardón a una deportista única e irrepetible: redefinió un deporte entero, el bádminton, con su desafío triunfal al imperio asiático
articles.summary: MARCA condecora con su gran galardón a una deportista única e irrepetible: redefinió un deporte entero, el bádminton, con su desafío triunfal al imperio asiático
articles.body: Arropada por los más allegados, su gente y su equipo, que tanto le ayudaron desde chiquitita en su ascensión al firmamento del deporte español, su familia, muchos de sus patrocinadores, Iberdrola e Interfresa, entre otros, los dirigentes que la han apoyado con firme convicción, como Alejandro Blanco, el presidente del COE, amigas ilustres y campeonísimas como la atleta María Pérez y algunos de los periodistas que contaron sus múltiples hazañas, Carolina Marín (Huelva, 1993), la mujer que redefinió el bádminton y desafió con éxito al imperio asiático, flamenca ella a más no poder, acaba de recibir en Madrid el MARCA Leyenda, la más alta distinción de este diario, el galardón que hace el número 99 de una lista fabulosa que inició en 1997 Michael Jordan y que tiene ya nueve mujeres, la flor y nata del deporte femenino mundial de todos los tiempos: Navratilova, Comaneci, Arantxa Sánchez Vicario, Sandra Sánchez, Ruth Beitia, Edurne Pasabán, Teresa Perales y Simone Biles. Ahora Carolina, raqueta en mano, con su épica, garra, perseverancia y su espíritu inquebrantable, se adentra con todo merecimiento junto a todas ellas por el soberbio 'Hall of Fame' de MARCA en un día agridulce, marcado por la tragedia de Tenerife por el fallecimiento del futbolista Jesús de Miguel. La emoción de Toñi, su madre, siempre sentida, que le entregó el trofeo, coronó un acto precioso celebrado en plena Gran Vía, en el emblemático Palacio de la Prensa, que sirvió para homenajear a la exjugadora de 33 años, retirada en marzo, para rendir cuentas a su luminosa trayectoria y celebrar su fantástico legado. ¿Quién jugaba al bádminton en España antes de Carolina? La luz de una cerilla en medio de una tormenta. Eso era este deporte en nuestro país hasta que llegó ella para hacer del granito de arena una galaxia entera. Capaz de conquistar en la victoria, con sus múltiples triunfos, algunos impensables para la niña que dejó Huelva atrás para soñar a lo grande y arrastrar al deporte español por territorios de victorias desconocidas, y de conmover en la derrota, cuando crujió su rodilla varias veces, alguna en plena competición, camino de una nueva medalla olímpica, como en París, Carolina lo recibió satisfecha y plena, leyenda de principio a fin, elegantísima, como es habitual. Humana, se acordó del drama del AVE de Urda y de Tenerife. "Quiero mandar un fuerte abrazo a los familiares de los fallecidos en el tren y también a la familia del futbolista del Tenerife. Estoy emocionada de recibir este premio. No es que se me ponga la piel de gallina, es que se me cae el moco. Es muy fuerte este premio. Al final los sueños se cumplen", comentó antes de dar un mensaje a los niños y las niñas que quieren ser como ella. "Hay que trabajar mucho, hay que tener dedicación y disciplina, y renunciar a muchas cosas. Hoy en la sociedad actual es difícil esto porque lo queremos tener todo", comentó antes de anunciar que quiere estar involucrada en el bádminton de muy diversas formas, "creando una academia y haciendo clínics". Durante la entrega, con el protocolo habitual en un día grande para MARCA pero al mismo tiempo consternados por el fallecimiento de De Miguel (hubo un sentido minuto de silencio), se repasó gran parte de su espléndida carrera. “Me gustaría contar cómo deslumbraste al mundo del bádminton con tu sobresaliente e inteligente manera de jugar. Cómo, además de destreza, has ofrecido durante tu brillante carrera una lección perpetua en lo táctico, lo físico y lo psicológico. Es verdaderamente indiscutible que te has ganado ser miembro de nuestra fascinante y deslumbrante relación de campeones. Tú formas parte de la cima para siempre. Formas parte, con protagonismo propio, de una época admirable y dorada para el deporte español en general y femenino en particular. Eres ejemplo, musa e inspiración para muchas niñas y niños que se miran en ti y que quieren ser como tú.”, decía Juan Ignacio Gallardo, director de MARCA, en su discurso. Campeona olímpica, campeona del mundo, campeona de Europa y de España, campeona por los cuatro costados, premio Princesa de Asturias, Gran Cruz del Mérito Deportivo y ahora MARCA Leyenda, Carolina, superlativa, lo ha ganado todo, con trabajo y sentimiento, de una manera muy especial. Así la definía Fernando Rivas, un entrenador capital en su trayectoria, el hombre que moldeó el talento y la ambición de la volantista andaluza, que moduló la voracidad de su agresividad competitiva y canalizó su frustración. Ella fue su gran creación deportiva. “Tengo un orgullo tremendo por la mujer en la que te has convertido, por ser un referente a nivel nacional y mundial.”, resumió Rivas. Pau Gasol y Saúl Craviotto se sumaron a la celebración con unos vídeos de felicitación y también Rafa Nadal, el ídolo de Carolina. Todos leyendas. María Pérez la definió como "un referente, la veía como alguien estratosférico, como un niño al ver a Cristiano Ronaldo" y Toñi, su madre, habló de "la niña" como un "torbellino" mientras recordaba cuando se fue rumbo a Madrid para vivir su sueño de bádminton. Mario Ruiz-Tagle, CEO de Iberdrola España, uno de sus grandes sponsors, le hizo entrega de un cuadro y Alejandro Blanco, presidente del COE, intentó calificarla, si es que es posible. "No sé cómo definirte, cuando te mandaba mensajes te decía eres la 1 y la única, y me quedaba corto. No se puede resumir lo que has hecho por el deporte español. Has roto todos los moldes de lo que significa el deporte. Has conseguido algo que ningún deportista va a poder ser. Nos han enseñado a ganar, a competir, a perder, a lesionarse y a levantarse. No habrá otra como Carolina". Un mito.

articles.title: Who is goalkeeper Owono and will he be punished after De Miguel’s death?
articles.summary: Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono is at the centre of a social media storm after the death of Tenerife’s Jesus de Miguel.
articles.body:
Jesus Owono has become a global figure overnight after the goalkeeper’s challenge led to the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

The 30-year-old died in hospital in Santa Cruz on Tuesday morning after suffering a cardiac arrest in the wake of a high challenge by Andorra goalkeeper Owono in stoppage time of Monday’s La Liga 2 game.

Owono received a straight red card for his challenge and has since received criticism from around the world for his part in the tragedy while local police are reported to have begun an investigation into the incident

The 25-year-old goalkeeper was born in Bata, Equatorial Guinea, but moved to Spain’s Basque Country as a child.

His first club was Antiguoko, a youth club in San Sebastian, at the age of eight, but after moving on to Real Sociedad, he played for the Basque Country’s representative side at under-16 level.

He joined Alaves in 2017 and worked his way through the youth ranks before making his first-team debut in a 1-1 draw against Real Sociedad in January 2022, becoming the first international born in his country to appear in La Liga.

He went on to make 20 appearances in the league and Copa del Rey but spent last season on loan with La Liga 2 side Andorra, keeping six clean sheets in 20 league games before earning a permanent move in August and signing a two-year deal.

Owono made his Equatorial Guinea debut shortly after turning 18 in March 2019 and has gone on to represent his country 46 times, playing every minute of their three group games in the 2025 AFCON edition and both their AFCON 2027 qualifiers against DR Congo and Sierra Leone in September.

After colliding with De Miguel in the centre circle, Owono did not turn back to look at his opponent on the ground but immediately began walking towards the touchline, anticipating the red card which Manuel Angel Perez Hernandez swiftly brandished.

However, as he walked off, after exchanging a handshake with teammate Nacho Quintana, he turned back as medical staff were beckoned frantically onto the pitch and jogged to join players surrounding De Miguel as he lay prostrate on the turf.

He remained on the field until he was led away by club officials and down the tunnel at the same time that De Miguel was being rushed off the field at the opposite end of the stadium on a stretcher to a waiting ambulance, with videos posted online showing Tenerife fans in the stands chanting ‘assassin’ at Owono for his part in the incident.

The reaction to Owono’s challenge on De Miguel is that it was widely considered reckless and using excessive force.

The keeper was standing well outside his area as 10-man Andorra piled on late pressure, seeking to complete an unlikely comeback from 2-0 down with just seven minutes of normal time remaining.

When the ball was cleared by Tenerife from the edge of their own box in the air towards the halfway line, De Miguel looked favourite to have a clear run on goal, leading Owono to sprint forward and jump to challenge him in the air before the ball bounced, with his knee appearing to strike De Miguel in the chest and head.

Some social media users have called for a life ban from football and criminal charges to be filed against Owono, while others have flooded his own profile with racist abuse, insults and comments of “murderer”.

Could Spanish football authorities punish Owono?

The Spanish Football Federation’s Disciplinary Code suggests a suspension of four to 12 matches for players found to have committed violent conduct during play, resulting in serious injury.

An investigation into the events surrounding De Miguel’s death will assess the challenge and the context in which it was made before determining the punishment.

Can a footballer be charged with negligent manslaughter?

While a severe sporting punishment seems inevitable, many football fans are suggesting that criminal charges should also follow.

Reports in the local media in Tenerife on Tuesday afternoon say The Homicide Group of the National Police in Santa Cruz is already investigating the circumstances of De Miguel’s death.

The death of a player due to an act on the field in the midst of a match is, thankfully, incredibly rare, and there are no precedents established in a tragic case like this.

The question of charges is likely to be determined by whether Owono’s challenge meets the threshold of criminal negligence.

Article 142 of the Spanish Penal Code distinguishes between manslaughter due to gross negligence and manslaughter due to less serious negligence.

Gross negligence, if proven, can carry a prison sentence of up to four years, while the lesser charge carries a fine calculated over three to 18 months.

articles.title: ISSF World Championships: India’s men win pistol team gold, women’s rifle trio bags silver
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable day at the ongoing ISSF World Championships on Tuesday, winning gold in the men's 50m pistol team event and silver in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India enjoyed a memorable day at the ongoing ISSF World Championships on Tuesday, winning gold in the men's 50m pistol team event and silver in the women's 10m air rifle team competition to take their medal tally to three.The men's trio of Ravinder Singh, Saurabh Chaudhary and Amanpreet Singh combined to score 1,659 to clinch the gold medal. Later, Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Uttam Maskar and Shambhavi Shravan Kshirsagar secured silver in the women's 10m air rifle team event with a combined score of 1,894.4.India are now placed second in the medal standings with one gold and two silver medals. China lead the table with five medals, including three golds.Ravinder leads men's team to gold, adds individual silverRavinder was India's top performer in the men's 50m pistol competition, shooting 559, including 11 inner 10s. Saurabh, a multiple-time World Cup gold medallist, contributed 551, while Amanpreet added 549 to take India's combined tally to 1,659.China finished second with 1,648, while South Korea claimed bronze with 1,643.Ravinder also secured the individual silver medal with his score of 559, finishing two points behind gold medallist Anton Aristarkhov of the Authorised Neutral Athletes (AIN), who shot 561. Romania's Luca Joldea claimed bronze with 558.The men's 50m pistol is not part of the Olympic programme.Elavenil qualifies for individual finalThe Indian women's trio finished behind China, who won gold with 1,899.8 points. Japan took bronze with 1,892.6.Elavenil was India's best performer in the qualification round, shooting 634.2 points. Sonam contributed 630.5, while Shambhavi added 629.7.Elavenil's performance also earned her a place in the individual final after she finished third in qualification. She will now have an opportunity to compete for an individual medal and India's first Olympic quota place at the championships.The men's 10m air rifle event, meanwhile, proved disappointing for India, with Rakesh Mane, Himanshu Dhillon and Paarth Makhija failing to make the team and individual finals.Doha offers first LA 2028 qualification opportunityThe championships in Doha are the first qualification event for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics and the biggest of the qualification cycle so far.A total of 36 Olympic quota places are available, with three on offer in each of the 12 individual Olympic shooting events. India did not have an opportunity to secure shooting quotas at the recent Asian Games, making this its first chance to earn places for Los Angeles.Each country can secure a maximum of one quota place per event at the championships, putting up to 12 Olympic berths within India's reach, according to the National Rifle Association of India (NRAI).Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
