articles.title: Nordic nations refuse to face Russia in ice hockey World Championship
articles.summary: Denmark, Norway and Sweden join Finland in refusing to face Russia in 2027 World Championships in Germany next May.
articles.body:
Denmark, Norway and Sweden say they would refuse to play against Russia in the ice hockey world championships next year because of its war in Ukraine, a day after neighbouring Finland said it would also refuse.

“The Norwegian Ice Hockey Association has decided that, based on the current situation and available information, Norway will not compete against Russia during the World Championships in 2027,” the association said in a statement on Tuesday.

“Our view that Russia should be banned from all international championships for the duration of the war in Ukraine remains firm.”

It said Norway would play its other group matches as planned.

The Nordic countries have been strong supporters of Ukraine since the start of the war.

Russia has been banned from International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) competitions since President Vladimir Putin launched the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

The 2027 world championships are due to be held in Germany in May, but the draw and scheduling for the tournament have already taken place, without Russia included.

The IIHF has voiced its opposition to the CAS decision and said it creates “significant practical implications”.

The head of the Danish ice hockey federation, Henrik Bach Nielsen, echoed that stance in comments to news agency Ritzau.

“For the sake of the integrity of ice hockey as a sport, we cannot see ourselves playing against Russia as things stand now,” he said. “It will end in chaos if we do.”

Sweden’s governing body for the sport said the same.

“The Swedish position is crystal clear,” it said in a statement. “It has been and still is inconceivable for Russia to take part in international ice hockey as long as the war in Ukraine continues.

“Swedish national teams will not play matches against Russian national teams.”

On Monday, Finland’s ice hockey federation said it would use “all possible means to prevent Russia from being reinstated at the world championships”.

“We are currently trying to rally as many countries as possible into a common front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia in the current situation,” said the federation’s president, Heikki Hietanen.

The Finnish city of Turku also said on Monday it would withdraw from hosting the junior ice hockey world championships in 2027-2028 if Russia were allowed to participate.

articles.title: Brooklyn Beckham's Halloween photo with Nicola Peltz and Damian Hurley takes unexpected turn after brutal third wheel comments
articles.summary: Brooklyn Beckham has removed a photo of his wife, Nicola Peltz, posing with their friend Damian Hurley after fans made fun of his position in the picture.
articles.body: Brooklyn Beckham has removed a photo of his wife, Nicola Peltz, posing with their friend Damian Hurley after fans made fun of his position in the picture. The three friends attended a Halloween party in Los Angeles, where Nicola and Damian wore similar black leather outfits while Brooklyn dressed as Superman. After the picture attracted comments calling him a “spare part,” Brooklyn edited his Instagram post, leaving only photos of himself and Nicola.Why did Brooklyn Beckham delete the photo of Nicola Peltz and Damian Hurley?Brooklyn, 27, shared a collection of Halloween pictures on Instagram on Sunday, November 1. One image showed Nicola, 31, standing close to Damian, 24, with his arm around her, while Brooklyn stood just behind them with his hands in his pockets. Their outfits also caught people’s attention because Nicola and Damian both wore black leather, while Brooklyn chose a Superman T-shirt with fake muscles and large glasses.The picture soon attracted comments from followers who felt Brooklyn looked out of place beside the pair. One person wrote, “Bless him he looks like a spare part,” while another said, “Brooklyn looks so out of place.” Someone else described the photo as giving a “3rd wheel vibe,” and another asked, “Why is she wearing a matching costume with some other guy?”Brooklyn later removed the picture from his Instagram carousel. The remaining post showed photos of him and Nicola together. However, the photo had already been shared elsewhere, including on Damian’s social media account, so people could still see the original image.Brooklyn also shared a separate picture of Nicola on his Instagram Stories, calling her “my girl” and adding Ariana Grande’s song Dangerous Woman as the music. He did not publicly explain why he removed the group photo, so the reason behind the edit has not been confirmed.What is the connection between Brooklyn Beckham, Nicola Peltz and Damian Hurley?Damian is the son of actress Elizabeth Hurley, and he has known Brooklyn since they were children. Their families have been close for years, and both Brooklyn and Damian have Sir Elton John as their godfather. The three also spent time together in Venice recently, attending celebrations for David Furnish’s 64th birthday.Damian showed support for both friends after their Halloween night out. He commented on Nicola’s Instagram post, writing, “i love you so much what a nighttt.” He also left a message under Brooklyn’s edited post, saying, “I love thiss the best night.”The photo discussion came shortly after Brooklyn and Nicola marked seven years together. They shared loving messages on social media, with Brooklyn calling Nicola his best friend and saying she meant everything to him. Nicola also posted a message, writing, “I can’t believe it’s been 7 years by your side, I wouldn’t wish it any other way.”Brooklyn later shared another photo of Nicola and wrote, “Yeah I am obsessed with my wife. Bring on the comments, I don’t care. She’s perfect xx.” The post came after followers had questioned some of their earlier public messages.The couple first reconnected at a Halloween party hosted by Leonardo DiCaprio in Los Angeles in 2019, after being introduced at Coachella in 2017. They married in April 2022 and renewed their vows in August 2025.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'I wasn't thrilled, I was disappointed': Why Dhinidhi Desinghu isn't celebrating her historic Youth Olympics medal
articles.summary: Dhinidhi Desinghu has created history for Indian swimming, but the 16-year-old is not entirely happy with her achievement.
articles.body: Dhinidhi Desinghu has created history for Indian swimming, but the 16-year-old is not entirely happy with her achievement. Her bronze medal in the women's 100m freestyle at the Youth Olympics in Dakar made her the first Indian swimmer to win a medal at the global event and opened India's medal account at the Games. Yet, the teenager admits she had set her sights considerably higher.Dhinidhi wanted to break the 56-second barrier or win gold. Neither target was achieved, leaving her with mixed emotions despite the historic podium finish."On one side, the expectation I had for myself was very different. I wanted to go below 56 seconds, which didn't happen though I was close, or win a gold medal, which also didn't happen. In that way, I wasn't thrilled; I was actually kind of disappointed," she told PTI from Dakar.Her final time of 56.27 seconds was, however, a personal milestone. It improved her own Best Indian Time of 56.57, set earlier this year, and underlined her progress in the event.'A very proud moment' for Indian swimmingWhile Dhinidhi was disappointed with not meeting her personal targets, she recognised the significance of her medal for a sport that has struggled for visibility and results in India, particularly in the women's category."But at the same time, bringing back the country's first medal. You would expect it in a different sport...you wouldn't expect from a girl who is a swimmer because swimming is nowhere and women's swimming is even more behind. So that way it is a very proud moment," she said.The medal is a landmark for Indian swimming, but Dhinidhi's journey on the international stage began well before Dakar. At 14, she was the youngest member of India's contingent at the 2024 Paris Olympics, having earned her place through the universality quota.However, she believes the Youth Olympics brought a different kind of competitive pressure."I didn't really think about it (being an Olympian). That's a much bigger meet. Like you're an Olympian already. So, you're coming to the Youth Olympics before the Olympics is like kind of funny. I didn't really think too much about the Olympics because I didn't really qualify. I was the best Indian. Yes, I got to go," she said.More pressure in Dakar than at Paris OlympicsDhinidhi explained that Paris was largely an opportunity to experience the biggest sporting stage, while Dakar offered a more direct test against swimmers she expects to face in the coming years."Here at the Youth Olympics, I'm competing against the exact people I will face in the future at the World Championships or World Juniors. Because of that, I actually had more expectation and pressure on myself to perform here than at the main Olympics. Paris was more for like the life experience of it and less of performance."Here obviously, we're looking at winning and doing well in terms of your time, coming back with medals. So, that way, it is very different. Youth Olympics is a little more pressure than the actual Olympics," she added.There is little time for Dhinidhi to dwell on her bronze, with two more events remaining, including the 200m freestyle, her main event. The 100m performance has given her confidence, particularly after improvements in her opening speed."I feel much better going into that. Because now I have a lot more opening speed. I have goals for that as well," she said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How sporting events are being impacted by Middle East conflict
articles.summary: BBC Sport takes a look at how the ongoing conflict in the Middle East has affected sporting events in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Bahrain and the wider area.
articles.body:
The 2027 Asian Cup is just the latest event to be postponed in the Middle East amid concerns about missile attacks by Yemen's Houthi movement.

The 24-team tournament - Asia's version of the Euros - was scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia from 7 January to 5 February next year.

The Asian Cup has now been delayed by almost a year , and will be held between 23 December, 2027 and 21 January, 2028.

Sport in the region had already been heavily affected by the US-Iran conflict, which led to the cancellation of the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian Formula 1 Grand Prix weekends in April this year.

Now the races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi at the end of the year are also in doubt due to that ongoing situation and the current conflict involving the Houthis. If they are cancelled, F1 would have lost four of its 24 events this year.

It is not just football and F1 that have been forced to cancel, reschedule or move high-profile events, and many more remain under threat.

BBC Sport takes a look at the situation across the sports.

The Saudi Pro League has, for the most part, managed to carry on as usual.

Several ​domestic ⁠league games had to be postponed, including three fixtures last month as the situation escalated.

The games were moved in the immediate aftermath of the attack on a major airport in Riyadh - though the SPL said they were switched "as a result of mandatory minimum rest periods between matches and to accommodate logistical requirements".

Following the postponement of the Asian Cup, this weekend's full round of Saudi Pro League has been called off.

The league once again has not attributed this to conflict in the region, instead saying the calendar would be recalibrated after the cancellation of the Asian Cup to achieve "a more balanced distribution of fixtures".

The AFC Champions League has been affected as well.

Cristiano Ronaldo and Kingsley Coman were among Al-Nassr's star players who did not to fly to Uzbekistan this week "given the pressure of matches and the amount of travel involved".

Al-Wasl of the United Arab Emirates also opted not to fly to Saudi Arabia to play Al-Nassr, and the match will be rearranged.

Meanwhile, the wife of Ollie Watkins, who plays for Riyadh-based Al-Hilal, posted on TikTok that she would be staying in the UK with their two children "until it calms down".

"We've had a bit of a plot twist," said Ellie Watkins. "I have come back to the UK for a little bit.

"There's just a little bit of conflict and things going on over in Saudi and we basically decided just to stay here.

"I felt like I needed to do that for the kids so there is some form of normality until we can get back out there and all be together."

Other well-known stars playing in the country include Gabriel Martinelli, Tijjani Reijnders, Darwin Nunez, Ivan Toney, Alexandre Lacazette, Ruben Neves, Sadio Mane and Joao Felix.

Formula 1 has a major dilemma about racing in the Middle East both at the end of this season and the beginning of next.

Most pressingly, the 2026 season is due to end with races in Qatar on 27-29 November and Abu Dhabi on 4-6 December.

As things stand, the sport is pressing ahead with plans to go to those races after being given security reassurances from various governmental sources that it should be safe.

There are, though, many people within the sport with misgivings about going.

Should the situation in the Middle East deteriorate in the next week or so, they could be called off and replaced with a single event in Imola in Italy on the Abu Dhabi weekend.

The 2027 season is scheduled to start in Bahrain on 12-14 March, with Saudi Arabia hosting on the following weekend.

But as things stand between Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni Houthi separatists, that race could not go ahead, and is likely to be cancelled if nothing changes by December.

Bahrain and Saudi Arabia are linked by a causeway, at the Saudi end of which is a facility belonging to state oil company Aramco, which has been targeted by the Houthis, while it joins Bahrain close to the F1 track.

One option being discussed is to hold that race in Malaysia, as was done in October this year.

The Dakar Rally was due to take place in Saudi Arabia in January but has been moved "following recent developments in the region".

Now the 2027 edition will begin in Loule-Faro in Portugal and end in Marrakech in Morocco.

Saudi Arabia had hosted the previous seven editions of Dakar, and the intention is to return in 2028.

Rally Saudi Arabia, part of the 2026 FIA World Rally Championship, which was scheduled for 12–15 November, has been cancelled.

But MotoGP will still take place this weekend at the Lusail International Circuit in Doha, Qatar, with three races left in the season.

It will go ahead without the Yamaha team, which has been advised against travelling from Japan.

The Six Kings Slam, which should have begun on Saturday in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, has been postponed by two months.

It is now scheduled to run from 27 December to 30 December at the ANB Arena, located about 31km away from the King Khalid International Airport, which was the target of an attack on 10 October that killed 13 people and injured 308 others.

Novak Djokovic, Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Alex de Minaur, Taylor Fritz and Learner Tien are due to compete.

But the 2026 WTA Finals, this weekend's season-ending championship of the women's tour, will not take place in Saudi Arabia.

A mutual agreement was reached to terminate a hosting agreement early, and it will instead take place at Indian Wells in the United States.

Saudi Arabia regularly hosts title fights and high-profile bouts.

Only last week, Mexican legend Canelo Alvarez reclaimed the WBC super middleweight championship against Christian Mbilli.

But the whole of the card did not survive as Lindolfo Delgado withdrew from his IBF lightweight title fight against Arthur Biyarslanov over safety concerns.

Next on the schedule is the Zuffa Boxing event, which will feature Carlos Adames against Welshman Gerome Warburton in Riyadh Season 13, on 14 November.

The WWE Crown Jewel 2026 event will still take place this weekend, but at a new venue.

It was originally scheduled for the Kingdom Arena, before being switched to the ANB arena.

The reigning men's and women's world champions of WWE's Raw and SmackDown face each other.

Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn, Liv Morgan, Chelsea Green, Bron Breakker, Austin Theory, Penta, Je'Von Evans, Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton are on the bill.

The FIFAe Finals, an esports tournament series organised by Fifa, should have taken place in Jeddah last month but was cancelled.

This week's UCI Urban Cycling World Championships, for the world's leading riders in trials and BMX Freestyle, in Riyadh was called off too, with a decision due "on the sporting consequences of this announcement".

The PIF Saudi International event, the season finale of the Asian Tour, will not be held between 18-21 November at Riyadh Golf Club.

After "an assessment of the organisational and logistical challenges associated with hosting the tournament" the decision was taken to call it off.

And on Tuesday, the Professional Triathletes Organisation said it was moving the Saudi Arabia T100 and World Triathlon Cup, in Jeddah, from the end of this month to 16-17 April.

articles.title: Ohio high school football playoff win erased after unusual ineligible-player scheme
articles.summary: A jersey swap between two players led 10-win Liberty (OH) having to forfeit its playoff win.
articles.body:
An unusual situation in Ohio has led to one high school football program having to forfeit its opening playoff win and the losing team getting another opportunity in the postseason.

According to a report from Josh Weir of The Canton Repository — part of the USA TODAY Network — Liberty (Youngstown, OH) has been removed from the playoffs after the team used an ineligible player in the team's 26-16 opening round win over Canton Central Catholic.

19News received further information, learning that the disqualification stems from an ineligible player swapping jerseys with an eligible player and playing in the game.

The report noted that Canton Central Catholic head coach Jeff Lindesmith was told that a fan of Liberty informed a Canton Central Catholic staff member of the swap. Liberty's athletic director Todd Smith was informed of the situation by that staff member shortly after.

Smith later reported the situation to the OHSAA, leading to Liberty's disqualification.

The Panthers entered the game with a 10-1 record and with the win, had advanced to a highly-anticipated second-round meeting with unbeaten Perry (OH). Now they'll have to look towards the 2027 season.

Meanwhile, Canton Central Catholic (7-4) now gets a new life in the postseason. The Crusaders will travel to Perry on Nov. 6 for their regional quarterfinals matchup.

Follow Sports Reporter Joe Spears on X at @joe_spears7 or via email: JSpears@usatodayco.com. For additional high school sports coverage, be sure to follow USA TODAY High School Sports on Instagram and X .

articles.title: Brazilian Grand Prix becomes a Minì-race at the last minute
articles.summary: Gabriele Minì will be back in action for Alpine at the Brazilian Grand Prix. The Italian will take over Pierre Gasly’s car during Friday’s first practice ses...
articles.body:
Gabriele Minì will be back in action for Alpine at the Brazilian Grand Prix. The Italian will take over Pierre Gasly 's car during Friday's first practice session.

Alpine's late announcement confirmed that this will be Gabriele Minì's second outing in the A526. The Formula 2 driver made his official F1 practice debut in Mexico and will take over Gasly's car this time.

Minì looking forward to a second opportunity with Alpine

Minì is pleased to be back in action so soon after his debut. The Italian hopes to build on the experience he gained in Mexico when he takes to the track at Interlagos.

"It's great to be back behind the wheel of the A526 for the second weekend in a row, this time in Pierre's car. Last week in Mexico City, driving in an official Formula 1 session was a fantastic first experience. It's great that I can build on that this week", said Minì.

The Alpine junior stressed that he wants to gain experience while also helping the team prepare for the rest of the weekend. "I want to put in some good laps at a very different circuit, Interlagos, and gather valuable data and information that can help us. At the same time, I want to keep improving myself," said the Italian.

articles.title: METROCARD SWIPE: Opening night payment declined
articles.summary: Merrimack loses early, and more notes around the Metro on opening day
articles.body:
Joe Gallo woke up at 3 a.m. ahead of Merrimack's opening game against App State. Team meal was completed by 3:33 a.m. But moments after Gallo's team took the floor at 6 a.m., he probably wished he could curl up in bed.

Todd Brogna picked up two early fouls; the Mountaineers had no problems breaking the zone and gashed it with shot-making. It was 16-3 at the first media timeout. It was 23-3 before Gallo called his first timeout.

From there, the Warriors won the rest of the game, but the deficit was too much. App State picked up a 63-49 win over Merrimack, dropping the reigning champs to 0-1 to start the new season. It all happened so fast.

"They were the aggressor on both ends," Gallo told Mid-Major Madness . "That's a really good defensive team. They provided really good resistance on that end, and I just think that led to our lack of defense as well."

The Warriors – like every other team — spent the offseason practicing against themselves. For Merrimack, that means seeing a zone defense every single day. On night one of the season, however, Gallo's squad faced a daunting man-to-man outfit.

App State has finished with the No. 1 defense in the Sun Belt two of the last three years.

"I think that athleticism and physicality was a little eye-opening," Gallo said. "To see that kind of defense in game one, which is obviously tough to replicate in practice."

On the rebound of the free throw after his first foul, he was whistled for another one. This season, Gallo is hoping to use Brogna as an offensive hub to take pressure off of his point guards. It'll look more like what it looked like at Stonehill.

But the Warriors couldn't get into any of that on Monday, and the burden fell on freshman starting PG Ayden Johnson, and his veteran backup, Felician transfer Jeremiah Anderson.

"I just think everyone was a little bit wide-eyed early," Gallo said. "You got a freshman point guard playing his first college game against a really good defense. I think that had something to do with it as well."

The Warriors found a rhythm, outscoring App State 46-40 after the initial 23-3 spurt, but Merrimack's season-opener goes down in the books as a loss anyway. Nobody had an efficient offensive performance. Not scoring leaders, wing transfers Denver Anglin and AJ Lesburt, and certainly not the point guards either.

Despite the resounding defeat, Gallo says he wants to return to the Field of 68 Tip-Off if he gets the chance.

Iona 56, Vermont 55 : In what was otherwise a pitiful opening night for the Metro Conference, Iona grabbed the league's only Division I win, taking down Vermont on a Kevon Vanderhorst game-winner. With 5 seconds left, just after Gus Yalden gave the Catamounts the lead, Vanderhorst took the ball from a timeout, went coast-to-coast, and laid the ball in with under a second to play.

Vanderhorst led all Metro players with 27 points, a new career high for the Drexel transfer, who looks like a superstar already. Dan Geriot was impressed with his scoring over the offseason, and we see why on opening night. He was the catalyst of everything Iona did on offense.

The Gaels did not do very much well on the offensive end. They're most-used lineup was Disu-Vanderhorst-Akametu-Ibine Ayo-Mitchell. That's not a very good offenisve group. There were a few minutes of lineups with Martin Kheil and Luke Jungers together, but most lineups that Iona threw out on the floor were defense-first.

Yalden went for 17 points, but the rest of the Vermont team struggled to enter the paint. They were just 6-16 inside the arc outside of Yalden, as Iona's deterrent five man, whether it's Mitchell or Alliou Fall, gave the Gaels defensive push. They held Vermont to .88 points per possession.

Dartmouth 69, Marist 62 : This is a bad loss for Marist. The Red Foxes had never lost to Dartmouth under John Dunne before Monday night, and this is projected to be the worst team in the Ivy League. Credit goes to first-year head coach Brett McConnell, but there are definitely things to be worried about for Marist on its home floor.

Myles Parker led Marist in scoring – but didn't attempt a two-point field goal. None of Jack Graham, Dywane Chess, or Edward Onyia broke into double figures. Jadin Collins-Roberts was forced to do more offensively, and he turned the ball over seven times. Marist only put up 0.89 points per possession.

"He didn't play up to his potential," Dunne said of Collins-Roberts. "Part of that is probably fatigue in the first game of the year, in front of the crowd, working so hard."

Marist needs more than just shooting from Parker, and it needs one of Chess, Graham, or Onyia to emerge as a big time scorer as well. Right now, the Red Foxes have no alpha, You can criticize their offensive efficiency over the last few years all that you want, but they've always had somebody to go to to take a tough shot late in the clock. It was Max Allen, then it was Josh Pascarelli, then it was Justin Menard.

Who is this team's guy? Is it too early to panic, I'd say yes. But my eyes are open.

Bryant 80, Siena 75 : Siena led by 11 points in the first half, and it looked like the Saints were going to run away with the opening night game against a tough Bryant team on the road. But Keegan Harvey willed the Bulldogs to victory. He battled with Tim Ibukunoluwa down low, each putting up a 20-point, 10-rebound double-double.

Ibukunoluwa though, has the license to do much more than simply battle down low. He's brought the ball up, made ambitious passes, attempted a bunch of threes (as did Harvey), and was all over the floor. He also turned the ball over eight times trying to do that. Nevada Smith wants to play with chaos. He's fine with effort or process turnovers if the Saints continue to play hard.

He's also emphasizing the three-point shot. They weren't falling for the Saints on Monday. Siena shot 6-for-27 from threee. Brendan Coyle made two, but Reid Ducharme was 1-for-4, and Pace Prosser was 1-for-5. Freshman Trent Egbiremolen was 0-for-6.

More importantly, Siena shot just 21-for-32 from the line. Parrish Edmond, who had a massive poster dunk in the second half, was 0-for-5. The Saints dealt with turnovers, poor shooting, poor foul shooting, and got out-rebounded by a massive Bryant team, and yet, they had chances to win the game.

They'll be around. This isn't a great loss for a team that we expect to be one of the best teams in the Metro, but it's certainly not as bad as Marist's.

Michigan State 96, Quinnipiac 59: The Spartans held Quinnipiac to .82 points per possession. The Bobcats shot 6-for-21 from 3, which is probably not too far off from their average night this year. They just won't be able to keep up with high-major athletes, and they're gonna win games with athleticism.

West Virginia 91, Niagara 46 : Niagara led 16-6 after nearly six minutes. Nothing after that counts.

Pitt 95, Rider 57 ; Rider scored just .77 points per possession. They were 11-for-33 inside the arc against Pitt's dual-rim-protector starting tandem. The size mismatch just hurts a team that will want to play smaller lineups.

Xavier 97, Mount St. Mary's 52: The score honestly doesn't even do justice how big of a rout this game was. The Mount was down 39-5 in the first half. They shot 3-for-26 from three and turned it over 19 times.

Seton Hall 66, Saint Peter's 42 : Saint Peter's had no way of scoring in this game. Seton Hall manhandled them inside the arc, forced 16 turnovers, and didn't send them to the line very much. It's a little disconcerting for an SPU team that I thought had some better offensive pieces, but Seton Hall is always a tough team.

Penn State 97, Canisius 57 : After two high-scoring exhibition performances, Canisius dropped a dud against Penn State. Michael Wilson, who scored 25+ in both exhibitions, scored just six points.

Sacred Heart 111, Coast Guard 44 : Number on the board. The Metro did not lose to a Division III school on night one. Jojo Wallace came off the bench and scored 21 points to lead a SHU rout.

The buy games aren't bad losses, per se, but there wasn't a ton of positives to go around the league within them. Night one was not great. Night two, with Manhattan visiting Kentucky, probably won't either. We'll learn a lot more about these teams in the Metro-America East Challenge on Thursday and Sunday.

articles.title: Hemric and Eckes Return to McAnally-Hilgemann Racing Truck Program in 2027
articles.summary: McAnally-Hilgemann Racing has locked in a couple of drivers for the team’s 2027 NASCAR FedEx Freight Truck Series driver lineup. On Tuesday, the organization...
articles.body:
McAnally-Hilgemann Racing has locked in a couple of drivers for the team's 2027 NASCAR FedEx Freight Truck Series driver lineup. On Tuesday, the organization announced that Daniel Hemric and Christian Eckes will return to drive the organization's No. 19 (Hemric) and 91 (Eckes) Chevrolet Silverados next season.

According to a press release from the team, NAPA Auto Care will serve as a primary sponsorship partner for both drivers and teams. This will mark the 37th year of partnership between NAPA and team owner Bill McAnally.

Columbia Bank and Motion will also return to the team in what the team calls "increased involvement."

While the 2026 campaign started off sluggish for Hemric, the driver was encouraged by the improvement down the stretch, and he's excited to return for the 2027 season.

"Our No. 19 team and the company certainly got stronger as the year progressed", Hemric said. "All our partners, NAPA, Motion, and Columbia Bank, have given us a great chance to build together in 2027. There is plenty of hunger internally to build the right culture and prepare the right way for a strong start next year."

With one race remaining in the season, Hemric, the 2021 NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series champion, has three top-five finishes and 11 top-10s in a season that he made The Chase.

Eckes is just thrilled to have next season figured out, and he feels confident that he and his No. 91 team can take a step forward in 2027.

"It's nice to have 2027 planned out already", Eckes said. "We want to accomplish much more in '27 than we did this year and feel strong about the plan we have in place to do it. The speed we've generated in the second half of this season has given us a lot of confidence to start next year strong and make the most of the opportunity with NAPA, Columbia Bank, and Motion."

Eckes, a nine-time NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series race winner, has nine top-fives and 15 top-10 finishes this season, heading into this weekend's season finale at Homestead-Miami Speedway.

articles.title: Napoli star Scott McTominay returns to Scotland squad for do-or-die Nations League deciders
articles.summary: Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli has received a significant boost ahead of the final international break of the year with the return of several key st...
articles.body:
Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli has received a significant boost ahead of the final international break of the year with the return of several key stars. Midfield powerhouse Scott McTominay has been included in the 26-man squad for the upcoming Nations League double-header.

The most significant news for the Tartan Army is the inclusion of McTominay, who makes his return to the international fold following a successful heart procedure. The Napoli midfielder has quickly rediscovered his best form in Italy, showing no signs of rust as Scotland prepare for two fixtures that will define their standing in the current UEFA Nations League campaign. His presence adds much-needed physical presence and goal-scoring threat to the middle of the park. McTominay has already scored four goals in seven appearances since his recovery, highlighting how vital he remains to the national setup

Joining McTominay back in the squad is Torino forward Che Adams, who was unavailable for the previous camp due to an adductor injury. Adams has been in impressive form in Serie A, and his return provides Pocognoli with more options in the final third. The head coach will be looking for Adams to lead the line with the same intensity he has shown in Italy, especially given the high stakes of the upcoming home match against North Macedonia and the trip to Switzerland.

While the returning players dominate the headlines, captain Andy Robertson is on the verge of making history. The Tottenham Hotspur full-back recently reached the 101-cap milestone, joining the legendary Sir Kenny Dalglish as only the second male player to do so. If Robertson features in both matches during this international window, he will move to 103 caps, officially becoming the most-capped male player in Scotland's history.

Robertson's leadership will be tested as Scotland navigate a difficult path in League B. The team currently sits in a position where two victories are almost certainly required to secure a promotion play-off spot. Alongside him, AFC Bournemouth's Ryan Christie is also approaching a personal milestone, with the midfielder set to earn his 75th cap if he plays in either of the two scheduled fixtures this month.

Pocognoli has largely stuck with the group that featured in the last round of fixtures, but he has introduced one fresh face to the senior environment. James Penrice has been rewarded for his versatile performances at Rangers, where he has featured both in the backline and across the midfield. His inclusion offers tactical flexibility for a coaching staff that is keen to find the right balance between defensive solidity and attacking flair.

However, the squad is not without its casualties. Defensive mainstay Scott McKenna and experienced midfielder Kenny McLean both miss out through injury, leaving gaps that the returning Kieran Tierney will be expected to help fill. The squad has been trimmed to 26 players, a slight reduction from the 28-man pool used previously, as reported by the Scottish FA.

Permutations for Nations League promotion

The objective for Scotland is clear but challenging. After a mixed set of results in the previous window, which included a win over North Macedonia but a disappointing home defeat to Slovenia, the pressure is on to perform. A minimum of four points is likely needed to keep the dream of promotion to League A alive, while anything less could leave the team looking nervously at the relegation spots.

The first hurdle comes against North Macedonia at Barclays Hampden, a venue where the fans will be expected to play a major role. Following that home clash, the squad will travel to face a strong Switzerland side.

articles.title: ‘They stink’: Former Cowboys quarterback calls his old team ‘absolutely embarrassing’
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys suffered another brutal loss on Sunday, blowing a fourth-quarter lead before falling to the Arizona Cardinals in overtime. And one of thei...
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys suffered another brutal loss on Sunday, blowing a fourth-quarter lead before falling to the Arizona Cardinals in overtime. And one of their former quarterbacks didn't hold back.

Ben DiNucci, who spent two seasons as a backup quarterback with the Cowboys and now works as an analyst for CBS Sports, called the loss "absolutely embarrassing." He also said simply that the Cowboys "stink."

The Cowboys led the Cardinals 14-3 at halftime and 24-10 early in the fourth quarter. But Arizona scored 20 points in the fourth quarter, tying the game on a Gardner Minshew touchdown pass to Michael Wilson with six seconds left.

Minshew came on in relief of starter Jacoby Brissett, and according to Awful Announcing , he hadn't completed more than three passes in a game since 2024. Arizona kicker Chad Ryland missed the extra point that would have won it in regulation, but the Cardinals kicked a field goal in overtime to win 33-30.

The loss dropped Dallas to 3-5. Jerry Jones has said he isn't planning to make a coaching change , but criticism of the team has been piling up. Cowboys legend Michael Irvin even said on First Take that his dead mom could coach them better .

DiNucci, who was drafted by the Cowboys out of college and spent the 2020 and 2021 seasons with the team, didn't sugarcoat things in his reaction on CBS Sports.

"This was absolutely embarrassing today. They stink. I'm lost for words honestly. They have so much talent on both sides of the ball, and year after year, week after week, all we see is just let-downs from them. I'm not sure what needs to change," DiNucci said, in a clip shared by Awful Announcing .

He went on to say that something has to change in Dallas, though he wasn't sure exactly what.

"At some point the same-old, same-old in Dallas for the Cowboys, it's not cutting it. Something needs to change. Somebody needs to look in the mirror. I don't know who it is. But that was an embarrassing loss. They had a 10-point lead with a couple minutes left. They let Arizona drive the length of the field a couple times. Tied that thing up. Should have lost in regulation, ended up losing in overtime. This is embarrassing for the Cowboys. Embarrassing," DiNucci said.

Clearly, Cowboys fans aren't the only ones who are fed up.

articles.title: James Hagens, Marco Sturm Break Down Rookie's Hot Start to Season, What's Next in Development
articles.summary: Boston's former No. 7 pick has impressed in his first 16 games this season, becoming a key weapon.
articles.body:
The Bruins seem to have found a rising star.

Through his first 16 games this season, James Hagens is building an early case to win Rookie of the Year, helping lead Boston to its sixth-straight home win on Monday night.

Hagens scored one of three Bruins goals, up to 12 points already as he's emerged as a key piece already, turning 20 years old on Tuesday.

Here's what Hagens and head coach Marco Sturm had to say about the rookie's emergence over the first weeks of the 2026-27 season.

James Hagens, Marco Sturm Break Down Rookie's Hot Start to Season

Through 16 games, Hagens now leads all NHL rookies in points (12). He's tied for the rookie lead in goals (6) and tied for second in assists (6).

On Monday night, the Bruins' 2025 No. 7 pick played a career-high 17:27 in his team's shootout win, giving his team a 1-0 lead in the first period.

When asked how Hagens can continue to develop, Sturm said postgame that he likes that Hagens is now "facing the big boys."

"That's something I can't even answer [for] you. It's just, overall, he needs to grow, as a player and as a person. Sometimes you have to be patient in that. I do like that now he's facing the big boys. I think those are big steps for him," Sturm said. "Moving forward, how to play, how to play behind him, how to manage pucks, not give away pucks. He can't do things overnight, but it has to be step by step, and sometimes it's just playing games."

"I think we all, especially Kells (Chris Kelly), do a good job sitting down with him one-on-one a lot and going through that stuff. I know his linemates are too, so we're just going to take it day by day and try to improve him in every area."

In the Bruins' last matchup against the Blackhawks, Hagens had a late turnover that led to Chicago extending its lead. But Sturm said the rookie has been quick to acknowledge his mistakes and move on.

"What I like about Hagens is that he knows. A lot of times," Sturm said, per The Athletic. "Not just about (against Chicago), but even the nights before. When he makes a mistake, he owns it. A lot of kids don't. He's willing to come in and watch it over again. It's a learning process for him as well. What I like about him is he's willing to get better and he realized a big mistake. Good for him."

While Sturm seems to be taking a patient approach with Hagans, the rookie's skill set has already put him at the top of Boston's roster.

"There's still a lot to grow," Sturm said, per The Athletic. "But he's getting it. He's getting it. That's the biggest thing. He knows now. As soon as he screws up, he's the first one that admits it. That's a good thing. You've just got to give him time. He's doing just fine."

After Monday's win, Hagens said he's feeling more comfortable in the NHL with every game that passes.

"It's nice to be here. It's nice to be a part of this, and day by day you feel more comfortable and that comes with just the guys in this room," Hagens said. "They were so welcoming to me and just to be able to come in here, and everybody has a smile on their face. It's fun to be around here. It's exciting and it leads over to the ice."

Hagens and the Bruins continue their season on Thursday against the Penguins.

articles.title: Global Hockey Heavy Hitters Refuse to Play Reinstated Russia
articles.summary: Finland, Sweden, Norway, and Denmark all refuse to play Russia.
articles.body:
Russia's reinstatement to International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) competition has already caused waves throughout the international hockey community.

The Court of Arbitration for Sports (CAS) ruled Friday that Russia must be allowed into international ice hockey competition for the first time since its invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The decision overturned an IIHF ban, which was centered on the fact that including Russia would raise safety concerns.

The IIHF said last week it was "disappointed" by the decision, but that it will abide by the ruling . However, an increasing number of key countries participating in elite international hockey competition have refused to play games against Russia in the 2027 men's World Championship if it participates.

The most notable nation is the hockey stronghold Finland , which won the 2026 men's World Championship in Switzerland. The Finnish city of Turku is expected to host the 2028 men's World Junior Championship, but has threatened withdrawal .

Sweden, Norway , and Denmark have also released statements that they vow to not play against Russia if they are included. And in Latvia , national law forbids sports teams from competing against Russia.

Germany, which will host the 2027 World Championship, hasn't officially announced it will not play against Russia if it competes, but it is considering pulling out as the host nation due to security concerns and associated costs. Several countries hosting upcoming IIHF events, including Canada and Czechia, have also said they will restrict entry and visas for Russian athletes.

Additional countries may refuse to play against Russia or adopt restrictions. Finland is reportedly among the countries lobbying other participating nations to decline participation as well.

The decision has also sparked commercial backlash, including from Swedish workplace furniture manufacturer AJ Produkter, which has been a major sponsor of the men's World Championship for the past 37 events. The company, whose logos have appeared on boards and referee jerseys, will not show its brand at the 2027 event.

The CAS's decision also has the potential to affect the World Cup of Hockey in February 2028.

The event, which is returning for the first time since 2016, is jointly operated by the NHL and NHLPA, and is not governed by IIHF guidelines. That leaves it up to the league and players' association to decide whether to include Russia in its eight-team competition field. It's not yet clear whether the pushback to Russia's reinstatement at IIHF events will affect the way the NHL and NHLPA will consider the country's participation, and there is plenty of time to see how the global reaction shakes out to make any decisions. The NHL and NHLPA both did not immediately reply to requests for comment.

The IIHF ban on Russian competition was put in place Feb. 28, 2022, and has firmly lasted. (The sanctions also included Belarus, though it's not clear at this point whether the country remains banned as well.) The policy is a stark contrast to the IIHF's ban on Israel in 2024 , which lasted about a week.

articles.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
articles.summary: Jarrel Comer, a former basketball player who quit football after middle school, has become a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State after a standout jun...
articles.body:
CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he's a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State .

Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California.

He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years.

"I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today," Comer said.

He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring.

At 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds, Comer was dominating in junior college from his athleticism alone. He didn't know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance.

"They didn't ask much of me," Comer said. "They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback."

What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU's fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush.

"His athleticism is off the charts," defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. "We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he's seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things."

Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. He credits MacIntyre and edge coaches Joe Seumalo and George Frazier with helping him learn the game, particularly pass coverage.

Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won't be able to focus all their offensive line on one side.

"Teams have to respect his speed," Hickle said. "If they don't, then he'll run right by them. He is definitely a threat in coverage and in the pass game."

articles.title: ESPN projects Pirates' Brandon Lowe to get an $80M contract despite three big questions
articles.summary: These questions about Lowe's game might not stop the Pirates' 2B from cashing in.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Pirates have some very interesting questions to answer this offseason after a promising 2026 season fell short of the playoffs.

After such a promising season, will the Pirates make a push to add talent this offseason, or will they continue to penny-pinch as they have for years now? There is one player this matters for more than any other: second baseman Brandon Lowe.

ESPN's Kiley McDaniel projected Lowe would get a four-year, $80 million contract this offseason, and that's despite the infielder having three big question marks looming over his free agency this offseason.

Brandon Lowe projected to get $80M contract despite three big question marks

"8. Brandon Lowe, 2B... Projected contract/QO: four years, $80 million (20 AAV), received QO," McDaniel writes. "... will he stay healthy, keep hitting this well, and continue to defend like this as he turns 33 in July?"

Those three questions surrounding Lowe's game will make his free agency very interesting to follow. Depending on how a team answers those questions, Lowe could see a huge swing in his contract value.

Even if some teams don't believe his defense will remain elite, as long as he's a great hitter and can stay healthy, he's sure to get very strong contract offers.

But if there is a team out there that believes Lowe can stay healthy, continue to hit at an All-Star level, and field as well as he did this past season, then he could see quite the strong offer this offseason.

Of course, the Pirates' placing the qualifying offer on Lowe does indicate they have interest in bringing him back, so the team that might believe in him could be the Pirates as opposed to some other club.

At some point, the Pirates do need to put together a contending roster and get out of their lengthy rebuild.

Re-signing Lowe would prove to the fanbase they're ready to contend, and if they believe in Lowe's 2026 being who he really is, then an $80M, four-year deal would make sense.

It's a lot of money for the Pirates, or any team, but if that team believes his offense, defense, and health are trending in the right direction, then this would be a worthwhile contract to give the 35-homer second baseman.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Matches Kobe – But Can He Pass Him?
articles.summary: Luka Doncic became the first Laker since Kobe Bryant to score 20+ points in five straight halves. The stats from Monday night prove the hype is real.
articles.body:
This historic run happened during the Monday night home game against the Miami Heat on November 2, 2026. The 24 points he scored by halftime sealed the deal and placed his name right next to the late legend in the franchise history books.

The numbers from this season are staggering and hard to ignore. Doncic is now averaging 37.7 points per game, which stands as the highest scoring average in league history for anyone who is not Wilt Chamberlain. He joined Bryant as the only two players in Lakers history to record at least 10 quarters with 20 or more points since the year 2000. Bryant had 36 such quarters between 2000 and his retirement in 2016, while Doncic hit his 10th mark during Friday's road game against the Warriors, where he scored 21 points in the opening quarter alone.

Fans often get lost in the flashy shots and ignore the work happening on the other end of the floor. Coach JJ Redick made sure to point out that the team was just as impressed by his defensive effort as his scoring. Redick told reporters before the game, according to the New York Post , "He's been awesome on defense. I think, even just his on-ball throughout this early stretch of games has been really good just in terms of containment." He admitted that watching the film from Sunday night showed how much the team was in awe of his defense during the actual game. The coach called the performance inspiring and said he really meant it.

This focus on defense separates good players from great ones. It is easy to shoot a ball, but it takes real effort to stay in front of a fast opponent. The fact that a player averaging nearly 38 points a game can also make a coach say his defense was awesome shows the complete package he brings to the court.

While Doncic was rewriting history, the Lakers also got good news about their starting wing. After missing three games because of left foot soreness, Ziaire Williams was removed from the injury report ahead of Monday night's clash. He last played on October 27 against the Trail Blazers, recording 11 points, 4 assists, and 2 steals in 29 minutes. Although Williams has struggled with foot soreness at the start of the season, the team is pleased to see him return.

Coach Redick gave a clear update on the injury status on Sunday. "The images have been clean," Redick said of Williams' foot. He described the issue as "a soreness that just pops up in the morning." The coach added that Williams is feeling much better, and they are just being cautious with the back-to-back schedule. Williams started in all four regular-season games he has played so far and is averaging 11.3 points on 57.1% shooting.

The only player left on the injury report was Adou Thiero, who was listed as out due to left knee injury management. With Williams returning, the Lakers have a stronger lineup to handle the tough games coming up. The team is coming off a win against the Raptors on Sunday night, which was the first night of the back-to-back set.

It is not just about the points. It is about consistency against the league's best teams. Doing this against the Heat at home is one thing, but doing it in back-to-back games against the Warriors and the Heat shows real stamina. The fact that he is the first to do this since 2007 means the gap between then and now was huge. Bryant set the bar high, and Doncic is clearing it without even looking down.

The media often talks about talent, but this is about work. The film sessions and the rep counts are what lead to these numbers. When a player puts in that kind of effort, the results show up on the scoreboard. The Lakers are getting a big return on their investment.
